An observer-based distributed control protocol using the information from the corresponding sensor buffer is constructed to guarantee the bipartite consensus of MASs. A numerical simulation is offered to illustrate the validity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Dynamic Parameter Identification of Industrial Robot Based on Improved Immune Clone Selection Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a method for dynamic parameter identification of unloaded industrial robots based on an improved immune clone selection algorithm (ICSA). Firstly, the dynamic model of serial industrial robot is constructed based on Newton-Euler method, and then the model is linearized. Secondly, the identification excitation trajectory is designed and optimized under the condition of satisfying the boundary constraints. Finally, in order to improve the convergence speed of the algorithm, the clonal mutation and apoptosis mechanism of the basic ICSA algorithm are improved. Simulation results show that the proposed method has better recognition performance compare with basic ICSA and least squares methods (LSM).

articleTitle: Navigation and motion control for micro-robot based on fuzzy-PID in blood-vessel mimic environment
abstract: In recent years, the research of microrobots in medicine has gradually matured. Navigation for micro-robot’s movement has also become important research. However, in the actual manipulation process of micro-robot, it will be disturbed by the flowing blood while moving in the blood vessel. Thus, the trajectory will be deviated from the predetermined one. In this paper, different algorithms were investigated for the navigation of micro-robot in blood-vessel mimic environment. Informed-RRT* was chosen as a better performed algorithm, according to the simulation results. With the pre-planned path, a fuzzy-PID controller was developed for precise trajectory tracking, which could effectively eliminate the random disturbance caused by the flowing blood during the movement process and enables it to quickly recover to a stable movement state.

articleTitle: Multi-AGV Simulation System Based on Bipartite Graph, Space-Time A*, and Conflict Search
abstract: Smart logistic industry prefers to use multiple AGVs for package dispatch. AGVs work in a pre-designed map of dispatching center, and are unified scheduling and planning by a high-performance centralized computing equipment. To proper function, these AGVs need to complete collision-free path planning in the map to reach their destination, and need to make a decision to return to a package entrance to pick up the package after completing the delivery. In this paper, we use optimal matching based on bipartite graph as the model of AGVs’ returning decision, and KM algorithm to solve the optimal matching iteratively using graph theory. For the collision-free path planning, we use space-time A* algorithm based on time stamp to search for conflicts in the space-time domain, and a binary search tree based on conflict search is used to find the collision-free optimal matching results as the upper layer of space-time A*. Additionally, we have integrated the two algorithms and placed them in a simulation system to visualize and evaluate the effects of the two methods on solving the problem. The algorithm shows good collision-free planning ability and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Unbalance control strategy for active magnetic bearing rotor system based on rotor unbalance mass identification
abstract: To improve the control accuracy and suppress the rigid rotor vibration, it is necessary to compensate for rotor unbalance force of the active magnetic bearing (AMB) rotor system. In this paper, the principle of rotor unbalance compensation is analyzed first. Then an unbalance compensation control strategy based on real-time identification of rotor unbalance mass position is proposed, in the new control strategy, the variable-step variable-angle (VSVA) iterative seeking method is used to search for rotor unbalance mass position to improve the seeking efficiency and accuracy. Finally, the search performance of unbalance mass position and the effectiveness of vibration control for the new unbalance control strategy are analyzed by numerical simulations. The results show that the rigid rotor vibration supression strategy proposed in this paper can effectively control the unbalance vibration of the AMB flywheel rotor system in constant speed state operation and variable speed operation , with the advantages of high search efficiency and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Enabling Inter-Agent Transfer for Multi-Agent Learning System by Incorporating Role Reversal
abstract: This work focuses on inter-agent transfer for multi-agent reinforcement learning. For a learning system consisting of multiple agents that cope with similar situations, incorporating inter-agent transfer could significantly improve the learning efficiency since the trajectories from others also benefit local policy iterations. However, experience sharing is typically not straightforward since the agents may have different sensors and observations. In order to transfer trajectories among agents, we propose to incorporate role reversal, which maps the observations of different agents and augments the experiences by exchanging their viewpoints. In this way, each agent learns from the trials of both itself and others. We further conduct simulations to validate the effectiveness, where the proposed algorithms surpass the baseline algorithms by a remarkable margin in all the situations. Importantly, our method can be integrated into all modern off-policy multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms to pursue better performance.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Surface Defect Detection Methods for Industrial Products
abstract: Compared with normal images, abnormal images have less proportion and higher acquisition cost. Thus, most existing methods are based on learning a normal image auto-encoding model. An image is considered to contain abnormal areas if it cannot be reconstructed well. Although this kind of method has made some progress, this framework can only ensure that the model can reconstruct the image as high as possible according to the input image, and cannot guarantee that the model can learn the ability to find abnormal areas in the input image. Naturally, if the neural network can learn abnormal data, the model will have better distinguishability. Addressing it, in this paper, we supplement abnormal data through data enhancement, which is trained together with normal data to realize self-supervised learning. Although the exceptions made by data enhancement do not perfectly simulate the real defects, the model can still learn a good ability to catch exceptions due to the generalization ability of deep learning. Besides, the ECA-Net is embedded into the backbone network which is capable of capturing complementary semantics and improving the accuracy of anomaly detection. In addition, CAM-loss drives the backbone to express the features of the target category, to obtain more discriminative feature representations that can get a better image-level localization by Grad-CAM. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments on the large-scale industrial product anomaly detection dataset (i.e., MVTec) demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: The Long-Term Primary Energy Consumption Structure Based On Carbon Neutralization
abstract: There are many factors affecting the long-term primary energy consumption. Moreover, these factors are nonlinear superposition. The factor of carbon neutralization is added to the model. In our work, I present an optimal synthesis method. This paper demonstrates an orthogonal coordinate system and displays a synthetization with the multi-factor. Therefore, I construct an orthogonal coordinate system. Therefore, each factor which affects the long-term primary energy based on carbon neutralization, can be decomposed and synthesized. It is obtained the trends about coal, oil, gas and non-fossil energy consumption finally.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Scheduling and Optimization of a PVC Plant: A Batch Based Approach
abstract: The calcium carbide Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) production process has the characteristics of mass production equipment, frequent product switching, continuous and batch production at the same time. It is critical to schedule the PVC manufacturing process for the Optimization of Process Operation and Energy Consumption. In this paper, we propose an integrated modeling and optimization method for multi-objective scheduling based on batch approach to address the problems of large model size, high dimensionality and the risk of exponential explosion in the PVC scheduling process. Firstly, the hybrid time description method is applied, the scheduling of PVC production is divided into batch decision making process and batch scheduling process, and the batch and multi-objective scheduling model is established with the optimization goal of minimizing the maximum completion time and production cost. Then, the distribution estimation algorithm is applied to optimally solve the scheduling model. The comparative results show that the integrated batch and multi-objective scheduling model reduce the completion time and total cost compared with the classical optimization model, and the model complexity is lower, which verifies the applicability and effectiveness of the model in the actual PVC production scheduling problem.

articleTitle: Neuro-adaptive Synchronization Control Design for Dynamically Positioned Marine Vessels with Unknown Input Gains
abstract: Dynamic positioning technology has become a critical support for offshore engineering operations with the increasing complexity. This study focuses on the neuro-adaptive syn-chronization control for dynamically positioned (DP) vessels with model uncertainties, sea loads, and unknown input gains. The synchronization control issue is reformulated as leader-follower configuration, with the objective of tracking the independent-controlled leader vessel in synchrony. Neural network (NN) techniques are applied in the backstepping control process to achieve the adaptive ability to the lumped uncertain dynamics. An improved adaptive control scheme driven by estimation errors is further introduced into the proposed finite-time neuro-adaptive synchronization control strategy. Given such a dynamic positioning control design, the synchronous tracking errors, adaptive control gains, and NN estimated weights can converge simultaneously within a finite time. In veiw of the proposed control scheme, it is theoretically guaranteed that the closed-loop system will remain semi-global practical finite-time stable (SGPFS). Finally, taking a shuttle tanker as an example, the simulation analysis verifies the designed DP control scheme.

articleTitle: A target association method for UAVs cooperative reconnaissance
abstract: Multi-UAVs cooperative reconnaissance will be one of the most important combat forms in future war. Target association is the basis of multi-UAVs cooperative reconnaissance and information fusion. The traditional methods are prone to false association when the targets are densely distributed. In this paper, a target association method based on image matching is proposed for UAV cooperative detection. First, each UAV detects the target by YOLOv5s. In order to overcome the impact of perspective differences, we compress and register the images at various viewing angles to create a unified coordinate system. Distinct from the traditional approaches, the method proposed in this paper is unique in that it only relies on the image information and takes the target detection results as the basis of association, rather than rely on the positioning data of the UAV to ground targets. In order to reduce the computational complexity of the algorithm, Minkowski distance is adopted as the similarity measurement criterion of position information. The information used for target association is only one compressed picture and the coordinates of the target detection results. The experimental results show that the proposed method has less information transmission, lower computational complexity and higher association accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Novel Underactuated Robotic Finger
abstract: In this article, a unique underactuated robotic finger is designed, which is composed of an underactuated planar linkage and a spherical four-bar linkage. The robotic finger can imitate the motion of a human index finger to grasp different objects. The kinematic model of robotic finger is established, and its workspace is analyzed. The relationship between the instantaneous kinematic of the internal four-bar mechanism and the first spring is derived using the screw theory. A prototype is designed, and its self-adaptability is evaluated through the experiment of grasping some daily objects.

articleTitle: Robust Event-triggered Model Predictive Control for Multi-Agent Systems with Switching Topologies
abstract: A robust event-triggered model predictive control strategy for multi-agent systems with random switching topologies is proposed in this paper. An event-triggered scheme is proposed to determine when state information of an agent is broadcast to its local controller and neighboring agents. A distributed control protocol is presented. The consensus problem is converted to the stabilization of a Markov jump system. Then a sufficient condition for leader-following consensus is derived. With a synthesis method to propose the robust controller and event-triggered weighting matrix, the objective function is minimized. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Optimization of Slab Location Selection with Markov Characteristics Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
abstract: The optimization of slab location plays a critical role in the management of slab yard, which is related to the efficiency of the subsequent hot rolling process. However, the current slab location recommendation still relies on manual recommendation. In order to realize the automatic production of iron and steel enterprises, a mathematical model that is more in line with the actual production process for the recommendation of slab location is established. And then, an improved genetic algorithm which can solve problems with Markov characteristics is designed to solve this model. Finally, using the data of actual production, the results of the improved algorithm and those of manual recommendation are compared, which proves the feasibility and effectiveness of the model and the improved genetic algorithm. The results demonstrate that the model has high value in practical application and can be used to improve the production efficiency of iron and steel enterprises. Meanwhile, the improved genetic algorithm proposed in this paper provides a new approach to solving problems with Markov characteristics.

articleTitle: Multi-stage Network with Garments Extraction Module to Improve Image-based Virtual Try-on
abstract: In the existing image-based virtual try-on works, the garment fabric is often wrongly retained in the neck, chest and some other positions. To deal with that, a multi-stage network with garments extraction module is proposed to enhance the quality of the generated images at the aforementioned area. The proposed network consists of four modules: the garment extraction module, garment warping module, semantic layout generation module and content fusion module. Our main work are the import of the garment extraction module and the improvement of the semantic layout generation module. The proposed method is evaluated qualitatively on the virtual try-on dataset VITON and a clothing dataset collected from the Internet which is mainly consists of hoodies and low necklines. Compared with the current virtual try-on networks CP-VTON and ACGPN, the proposed approach obtains more natural images especially in some specific areas such as neck and chest. Despite the addition of extra modules, our work cost only 0.02ms extra compared to ACGPN.

articleTitle: Single Machine Control for Energy Consumption Analysis in Bernoulli Serial Lines
abstract: The green development of the manufacturing is supported by energy conservation and environmental protection policies. The implementation of strategies has gradually expanded from a single field to multiple fields. These changes improve quality of products, innovation ability and efficiency of resource allocation of manufacturing systems. In recent years, reducing energy consumption has become the focus of both industry and academics. In order to save energy, we consider switching on/off a machine in the production lines when certain thresholds of buffers are reached. In this paper, we investigate Bernoulli serial lines with buffers having limited capacity which run finite production. Mathematical model of the three-machine line which produce finite products is established and analytical methods of calculating production rate, consumption rate, blocking probability, starvation probability, completion time and energy consumption are proposed. Markovian approach is adopted in three-machine lines analysis. Meanwhile, simulation is used to analyse serial lines that have numerous machines.

articleTitle: Scheduling control of the temperature profile of a catalytic rod
abstract: We address the problem of temperature-profile scheduling control on a catalytic rod model. Galerkin technique can be successful to reduce the infinite-dimensions temperature profile equation into a finite-dimensions equation. Then, we can get the state stability of the infinite-dimensions temperature profile equation through analysing the related finite-dimensions equation. To overcome the difficulty that the obtained reducing system is difficult to design controller because of its nonlinearity. Combing the Lyapunov analysis technique, a stability criterion with sufficient conditions is given and the controller gains are designed by linear matrix inequality approach. In the end, how to design schedulable controller gains is shown in the section numerical example simulation.

articleTitle: A GM-TCN based Hybrid Prediction Method for Ash Fouling Prediction in Coal-fired Power Plant Boiler
abstract: In response to the problem that ash deposition in boilers has a great impact on production efficiency as well as production safety, a grey level theory prediction model based on time convolution networks (GM-TCN) is proposed to predict the degree of ash in boiler heated areas by using a cleaning factor to assess the ash deposition condition on the heated surfaces. The accuracy of the prediction model is improved by utilizing the features of grey level theory that can predict the developmental changes in system behavior, combined with the high-precision approximation capability of the time-convolutional network. The modelling prediction of the ash level in the heated area of boilers during the production of coal-fired power stations is investigated. Experiments demonstrate that the model can predict the cleanliness factor with high accuracy, and the predicted values are closest to the true values compared to the other two models, verifying the accuracy and reliability of the model.

articleTitle: ActionFormer: Pose-based Action Recognition via Transformer and CNN
abstract: Recently, human pose estimation and human skeleton capture system developed rapidly and raised more and more attention to pose-based action recognition. Deep learning algorithms like CNN and RNN have been applied to many tasks for the past few years. Although they have showed promising prospects, these methods lack the ability to take full advantage of spatio-temporal relationship information between the skeletons in the behavior explicitly, and the accuracy of action recognition is not easy to improve. We put forward a new and effective CNN-Transformer model able to extract spatial-temporal information for human pose-based action recognition to address these problems. Firstly, we extract the pose features from the original video. Secondly, the pose features are processed by action modeling module. Then, we feed the spatio-temporal information of the skeleton points generated by the modeling into CNN and Transformer modules respectively, in the form of relative position and relative speed. Finally, the output information obtained from the two modules is fused. What is more, we compare the model with the previous advanced methods and carry out comparative experiments on SUB-JHMDB, SYSU-3D and NTU RGB+D datasets. It is obviously that the model significantly improve the action recognition performance through the experimental results.

articleTitle: Research on Formation Self-healing Method of Multi-agent System Based on Manta Ray Foraging Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Multi-agent systems are composed of a series of independent or interacting individuals. Faults are inevitable due to the fact that they often work in complex environments. Fault of agents in a formation can lead to degradation of system performance and efficiency, and if no action is taken, it may even cause serious consequences such as system collapse and formation failure. Therefore, it is important to recover the performance of the formation automatically when fault occues. To address this problem, a self-healing strategy and method based on multi-agent system formation failure is proposed. The optimal solution of current spatial agent distribution is solved by manta ray foraging optimization algorithm, and potential energy function is used to deal with the collision problem during agent movement And the coverage rate is used as an important index of self-healing performance by measure the self-healing effect of intelligent body formation before and after the failure. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the method in the self-healing of multi-agent formation is verified by a large number of simulations.

articleTitle: Terminal sliding mode control for rotary cranes based on Extreme Learning Machine
abstract: A terminal sliding mode (TSM) control strategy based on Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) is applied for the tracking control and load sway control of a rotary crane with uncertain dynamics. The disturbance observer is designed to compensate the unknown disturbance. Then the complex crane system can be divided into two linear models. The proposed control effectively estimates the lumped uncertainty by a neural network with ELM. For the problems of slow convergence and chattering, a terminal sliding mode surface is introduced to ensure the tracking error converge in limited time, and the continuous function is used to replace the sign function to eliminate chattering. Finally, the closed-loop stability and finite-time convergence are proved. The simulation shows that the method is robust to the changes of load mass and rope length of the crane system.

articleTitle: Research on software scheduling of spacecraft real-time system
abstract: The real-time performance and reliability of on-board software is significant for the Spacecraft. Due to the expansion of space missions and the growth on complexity of on-board software, implementing the software scheduling in the distributed on-board integrated computing system becomes an important research issue. A software scheduling method is proposed for embedded real-time system of spacecraft. It aims to solve the problems of multi-node redundant scheduling of safety-critical tasks and continuity requirement of software tasks, which has good application value for increasing efficiency of on-board software scheduling.

articleTitle: Robust predictive control for uncertain singularly perturbed systems
abstract: In this paper, In this paper, a robust predictive control problem for a class of uncertain singularly perturbed systems is studied. By using state feedback control, the specific design steps and methods of the new robust predictive controller are given. Firstly, based on linear matrix inequality method, Lyapunov stability theory, the optimization problem under linear quadratic performance index is solved online, and the constraints of the controller and a set of piecewise continuous state feedback control sequences are obtained. It is further proved that there is the feasible solution of the optimization problem at the initial time. On this basis, it is guaranteed that the uncertain singularly perturbed system is regular, stable, impulse free. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the method are verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Planetary Gearbox Using Modal Multiscale Spectral Features and 1-D CNN
abstract: The single-scale fault features of original signal from wind turbine planetary gearboxes cannot describe fault information comprehensively; instead, it generally leads to low fault diagnosis accuracy. Therefore, a fault feature extraction method is proposed for wind turbine planetary gearboxes based on the modal multiscale spectral features (MMSF) and 1-D CNN. In the feature extraction, the variational modal decomposition (VMD) is applied to gearbox vibration signal, and the intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) are obtained. These IMFs are subjected to the coarse-grained processing in the time scale. The fast Fourier transform (FFT) is performed on these IMFs, and the multiscale spectral features (MSF) of IMFs’ spectrum are extracted. Furthermore, the MMSFs are normalized and placed in the designed classifier based on 1D-CNN for training, the diagnosis modal is obtained to identify the different fault. The gearbox fault data is collected from the Wind Turbine Drivetrain Diagnostics Simulator. The experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the accuracy of gearbox fault diagnosis and has good practical value to monitor the health condition of the rotating machinery equipment.

articleTitle: A Fast Reconstruction Method Based on Real-time Terrain Following
abstract: Carefully planned flight trajectories for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) are used to reconstruct high-quality 3D models of real environments, which greatly simplify the process of large-scale scene reconstruction and reduce the computing cost. However, in order to better capture the image of uneven terrain in the strange environment, most state-of-the-art methods need a prior map of the scene, and thus additional pre-processing steps are required before the actual image acquisition. To address this limitation and make unknown landscapes easier to be reconstructed, we propose an algorithm for real-time exploration and reconstruction that does not demand any prior map of the area. And it can quickly generate dense point clouds for the area. The algorithm uses the sparse point cloud generated by Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) to guide the UAV movement, in addition it generate pruned dense 3D point clouds by constructing virtual stereo-pair from consecutive frame. Experiments show that the proposed method could generate effective flight trajectories that satisfy to the task, therefore, the 3D scene could be reconstructed quickly with comparable accuracy without prior map information.

articleTitle: Short-term Power Load Forecasting Method Based on VMD-ARIMA-SVR
abstract: Aiming at the problem of strong randomness and low prediction accuracy of power load, a short-term prediction decomposition and reconstruction model of power load based on differential integral moving average autoregressive and support vector machine is proposed. The grey wolf algorithm is improved by using the nonlinear control factor and the random weight position update strategy. The improved algorithm is used to optimize the kernel parameters and penalty factors of the support vector machine, and the integrated moving average autoregressive model is used to predict the data after the variational mode decomposition, and the final prediction value is obtained after reconstruction. Combined with the actual data prediction analysis in a certain area, this method has better prediction accuracy and convergence speed than other prediction models.

articleTitle: Tracking Performance of Networked Systems with Limited Bandwidth and Colored Noise
abstract: This study investigated the optimal tracking performance (OTP) of multi-input multi-output (MIMO), discrete- time networked control systems (NCSs). The limits of tracking performance (TP) under the influences of bandwidth, encoding- decoding, and additive coloured Gaussian noise (ACGN) are derived using the techniques of coprime decomposition and all-pass decomposition. The results reveal the negative impact of non-minimum phase (NMP) zeros and unstable poles of the plant as well as network communication constraints on the TP of NCSs. Finally, a numerical simulation is discussed and verifies our conclusions.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning for the Wheeled Mobile Robot Considering Diamond-shaped Velocity Constraints
abstract: The trajectory planning of a two-wheeled differential mobile robot with diamond-shaped velocity constraints is studied in this paper. First, the kinematic model and the diamond-shaped velocity constraints of the mobile robot is given. Then, the artificial potential field (APF) functions are established for the target point and obstacles in the environment map. By solving a series of constrained optimization problems, the global trajectory planning can be achieved. Finally, we use the cubic spline method and the model predictive control (MPC) algorithm to further optimize the planned trajectory to make it smoother and ensure that the diamond-shaped speed constraints are met. Simulation results present the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Finite-time control of singular nonlinear time-delay systems via Hamiltonian method
abstract: In this article, we study the finite time control problem for a nonlinear singular delay Hamiltonian system. First, the general nonlinear singular Hamiltonian system with delay is transformed into its equivalent Hamiltonian form. Then, through a designed state feedback controller, we obtain its strictly dissipative Hamiltonian form. The appropriate Hamiltonian function and Lyapunov function are selected to study the finite time stability of the dissipative Hamiltonian system. The paper presents a stability result on the delay system. It should be pointed out that, due to the existence of delay term, it is more difficult on the stability analysis for the singular system.

articleTitle: Trajectory Optimization for Urban Rail Transit Considering Regenerative Energy Utilization: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: Energy saving in urban rail transit (URT) has recently been developing vigorously. Regenerative braking is critical for reducing consumption in URT operation, especially when regenerative braking energy (RBE) recycling with high efficiency. This paper proposes a trajectory optimization to reduce traction consumption by means of reusing RBE. First, an electric energy computation model is developed to evaluate traction power on substation level, in which electric characteristic of traction power system is taken into consideration. Then, the train operation process is discretized and turned into a multistep decision optimization problem by defining the objective as a trade-off of RBE reusing efficiency and given running time. A Deep Q Network approach contains dense reward is introduced to solve it from a Reinforcement Learning perspective. Finally, some numerical studies based on real-world data are implemented to verify the effectiveness of proposed approach and algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Cooperative Scheduling System for Mobile Robots Cluster
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of robots cooperation in intelligent manufacturing, a cooperative scheduling system for mobile robots cluster was designed and built based on openTCS. The architecture and components of the cooperative scheduling system for mobile robots cluster were proposed and multi-robot collaborative SLAM was discussed. Furthermore, the scheduling system was built and tested in industrial material handling scenario. The test shows the system is compatible with various types of mobile robots and can complete material handling tasks efficiently, which has high engineering practical value.

articleTitle: MRAC-Based Adaptive Feedback Linearization Control Method for Continuous-Time Nonlinear Systems with Uncertain Parameters
abstract: The feedback linearization method can accurately linearize the nonlinear system. However, feedback linearization needs the exact dynamic of nonlinear systems, it is difficult to apply to unknown nonlinear systems. To be capable to perform the feedback linearization of the continuous-time nonlinear system containing uncertain parameters, a model reference adaptive control (MRAC) scheme is introduced in this paper. First, we construct a state feedback controller by the knowledge of the system model structure and form it into an adjustable system together with the nonlinear object. The reference model is decided upon to be a standard linear system. Second, based on the output errors of reference model and adjustable system, we adaptively modify the state feedback controller’s unknown parameters using the gradient descent approach. Finally, the simulations and real-world experiments on a first-order inverted pendulum system are carried out to assess the effectiveness of given methods.

articleTitle: Multiscale Deep Features and Empirical Features Fusion-based Gearbox Fault Diagnosis
abstract: The application of gearbox intelligent fault diagnosis techniques in engineering practice is still challenging. Based on a deep neural network, the accuracy and generalization ability of the diagnosis model cannot be guaranteed when the labeled data is insufficient. In addition, due to the complex internal structure and strong coupling of gearbox, it is unrealistic to obtain reliable and complete fault information with a single model structure. Therefore, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method for gearbox based on the fusion of multiscale deep features and empirical features, which can extract available information from various scales. The method combines traditional signal processing methods, multiscale learning and classical convolutional neural network (CNN) structure, which has two advantages. 1) Taking full advantage of the feature extraction of different techniques, multiscale learning strategies can obtain complementary diagnostic information to improve the diagnostic effect. 2) Variational mode decomposition (VMD) can obtain relatively stable signals, effectively dealing with the data noise problem that helps mine the fault characteristics of vibration signals. The performance on gearbox datasets demonstrates the superiority and robustness of the proposed method in gearbox fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Detection of Side Wall Protrusions in Highway Tunnel Based on LiDAR
abstract: The detection of sidewall protrusions in highway tunnel is significant for the intelligent cleaning of tunnel walls. An automatic detection method for sidewall protrusions based on LiDAR in the scene of long curved tunnel walls is proposed in this paper. First, the ground point clouds are removed by using cloth simulation filter (CSF) algorithm. Then, the obstacles point clouds are clustered by combining the region growing (RG) algorithm and the improved Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm. Finally, in order to separate wall protrusions and other obstacles, tunnel boundary is extracted by horizontally projecting the remaining point clouds after removing the ground point clouds. The experiments show that the proposed method in this paper can effectively detect the protrusions on the sidewall of the tunnel.

articleTitle: Effect of inlet mode on combustion and emission characteristics of rotary oscillating internal combustion engine
abstract: In order to study the influence of the intake method on the rotary oscillating internal combustion engine, a numerical simulation calculation model of the working process of a suitable rotary oscillating internal combustion engine was constructed based on CONVERSE. The air intake mode is set to single nozzle mode and double nozzle mode, and the influence of different intake methods on the cylinder flow field, flame propagation and emission generation law of the internal combustion engine is analyzed by comparison, and the influence of the intake mode on the combustion process of the rotary engine is studied. The results show that the intake mode of the rotary swinging internal combustion engine will affect the turbulence intensity in the cylinder, thereby affecting the mixing of the mixture in the cylinder and affecting the propagation speed of the flame, but the turbulence intensity is too strong, and the flame surface will be broken, resulting in a decrease in the exothermic heat; compared with the double nozzle intake method, the single-nozzle intake method can reduce the HC emission by 37.5%, which has a significant emission reduction effect.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Adaptive Neural Finite-Time Trajectory Tracking Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels with Input Saturation*
abstract: To eliminate the adverse effects of dynamic uncertainty and unknown external disturbances on the underactuated surface vessels(USVs) trajectory tracking system under the input saturation, a concise trajectory tracking control scheme is designed in this paper. The dynamic uncertainty of the USVs is reconstructed by using the neural networks(NNs), and the minimum learning parameters(MLPs) is introduced to convert the uncertain dynamic of the system into a single-parameter learning form, which reduces the computational complexity of the system. The transient performance and steady-state performance of the system are improved by finite-time technology, and event-triggered technology is introduced to solve the impact of communication resource limitation on the system. A rigorous theoretical analysis is provided for the designed control scheme based on Lyapunov stability theory, and the effectiveness of the control scheme is verified by simulation. The simulation results show that the control scheme designed in this paper has good steady-state performance and high tracking accuracy, and effectively saves communication resources.

articleTitle: Linear Optimal Strategies for LQ Difference Game with Packet Losses*
abstract: This article investigates the optimal linear solutions for the finite horizon stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) difference game with two players over a TCP-like lossy networks. One player’s control and its actuator channel has packet losses, while the other player has not packet loss. We first provide a optimal estimator of the state, and then give some conditions based on the packet loss rates under which the optimal controller exists.

articleTitle: Multimedia-based Camera-Laser Joint Calibration
abstract: Line structured light measurement systems are widely used in the 3D model reconstruction in air. When deployed in a multi-media scene, the measurement system will not work effectively due to the failure of general imaging models. To solve these problems, we propose a multi-media-based 3D reconstruction method, in which applying the calibration parameters in the air and considering the refraction of light can improve the accuracy of 3D reconstruction in multimedia without recalibrating sensor parameters. With the help of the system experimental platform, the practicability and accuracy of our proposed method are verified by comparative experiments under common multi-media conditions, respectively.

articleTitle: The generalized synchronization for double-layer delayed coupling complex networks by dynamic soft variable structure control method
abstract: This study focuses on the synchronization problem of double-layer complex networks with time delayed coupling. Distinguish from most of previous works, a more general network model is introduced, where the number and the dimension of the nodes can be different between the drive network and the response network. This network model is more close to the practice. In order to obtain the synchronization of double-layer complex networks, an ingenious dynamic soft variable structure controller is proposed, where three sub-controllers and one adaptive observers are designed, and the stability of the controller is demonstrated by a strict mathematical proof. Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Application of Model Compression Technology Based on Knowledge Distillation in Convolutional Neural Network Lightweight
abstract: Nowadays, the neural networks become deeper and deeper, the number of parameters has continued to increase and the complexity of model has also continued to increase. These models are difficult to deploy in embedded devices, consequently the lightweight of deep neural networks is particularly urgent. To solve these problems, knowledge distillation comes into being. Through knowledge distillation, the model can be simplified. This paper discusses knowledge distillation, a relatively flexible and efficient model compression method, describes how the deep neural networks developed and the development of knowledge distillation technology, and then introduces the method and principle of knowledge distillation in detail. We accomplished experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset and the distillation results at different temperatures were obtained to achieve the certain results of knowledge distillation. Finally, the future development of this technical method was prospected.

articleTitle: Research on Power Quality Signal Reconstruction Method Based on Compressed Sensing
abstract: The phenomenon of power pollution is becoming more and more seriously, on account of the theory of compressed sensing, it is of great significance to the research of power quality disturbance signal recognition. To solve the problem of the current power quality signal reconstruction algorithms are not adaptive and low reconstruction accuracy, the sparse adaptive algorithm is proposed to apply to the power quality signal reconstruction. DFT basis is selected as the sparse basis, observation matrix is designed as binary block diagonal matrix and SACoSaMP algorithm is proposed to reconstruct the power quality signal, which uses recursive to dynamically adjust the real sparsity of the approximation signal through the change of residual. The experimental results show that, the power quality signals are reconstructed using the proposed algorithm, the SNR of all the reconstructed signals are higher than 32 dB, ERP are over 99.7%, and MSE are under 2.5%. The indexes of the proposed algorithm are obviously superior to the existing ROMP algorithm, which further verifies the superiority and applicability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on single image super-resolution algorithm based on region perception
abstract: In recent years, adversarial network-based research has made great progress in single-image super-resolution, In particular, the Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative adversarial networks (ESRGAN) can generate realistic and natural high-resolution images from low-resolution images. However, in the region with rich texture details, the super-resolution results generated by the existing algorithms are often unreal or inaccurate, and often produce artifacts. In order to improve the perception quality of detail texture region, residual paths are added to ESRGAN network structure to enhance feature extraction. To enhance the discriminator's discrimination ability for texture details, we propose a super-resolution training strategy based on region perception. To reduce artifacts, we analyze the source of artifacts and construct artifact loss according to the local statistical information of artifacts. Experiments show that the proposed super-resolution network based on regional awareness achieves better perception quality than the GAN-based SISR presented in recent years.

articleTitle: Controller Design for a Class of Nonlinear Discrete Networked Cascade Control Systems With Time-Varying Delay
abstract: The problem of a class of nonlinear discrete networked cascade control systems (NCCSs) with time-varying delay is studied. Firstly, a model of discrete NCCS is established. The secondary controller object is regarded as a nonlinear system, and a new NCCS model is established. Based on this model, time delay are fully considered, and two gain of proportional (P) controllers are co-designed by using linear inequality technique. Taking a thermal power plant as an example, the effectiveness of the proposed collaborative design method is verified.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Indoor Point Clouds with the Channel Attention Mechanism
abstract: In recent years, the semantic segmentation of 3D point cloud has received increasing attention the field of computer vision, because 3D point cloud can better reflect our 3D space. Because of the unstructured and disordered characteristics of 3D point cloud data, semantic segmentation of point cloud is still a difficult task. Our network automatically learns the importance of feature channels by adding a channel attention module, which enables the network to obtain better training results. After the channel attention module is fused, the important channels in the features are enhanced, and the unimportant channels are suppressed, making the network training more efficient. In this paper, we propose an indoor point cloud semantic segmentation method combined with channel attention mechanism. The experimental results show that our method achieves better results than other methods.

articleTitle: A Vibration Suppression Method of Series Elastic Actuator Based on Particle Swarm Algorithm
abstract: Series elastic actuator (SEA) are widely used in exoskeleton robots. For its vibration suppression problem, this paper proposes a method of "planning and controlling" in the SEA system. First, according to the kinematics constraint equation of the connecting rod, the position of motor is planned based on the second-order low-pass filter, which used particle swarm algorithm to optimize the filter parameters in the process. Second, a position tracking controller is used to make the motor accurately track the desired trajectory according to dynamical model of the motor. The optimal filter is finally found to plan the motor trajectory by iterative simulation based on particle swarm algorithm. The experimental results show that this "planning and controlling" method can effectively suppress residual vibration while ensuring that the connecting rod reaches the desired position accurately.

articleTitle: Input-to-State Practical Stabilization of Event-Triggered Switched Systems subject to Cyber-attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of input-to-state practical stabilization for switched systems in the presence of deception attack and denial of service (DoS) attack. To describe the relationship between subsystem and actuator since cyber-attacks impact on the actuator's update, we first construct the mixed switching signal combing the switching signal of subsystem with attack-induced switching signal of actuator under the different attack models. Then, under the proposed event-triggering scheme, the relationship between synchronous and asynchronous durations caused by cyber-attack can be established, which is used to develop the sufficient condition for input-to-state practically stability (ISpS) of such system. Finally, the feasibility of proposed result is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Day-ahead scheduling model for integrated energy system with demand response and responsible consumption weights
abstract: In order to improve the economy of integrated energy system operation and the level of new energy consumption, this paper proposes a day-ahead scheduling model for integrated energy system with demand response and responsible consumption weights. First, mathematical models of incentive-based demand response, customer satisfaction, responsible consumption of new energy as well as each device are constructed based on mathematical methods. Second, objective functions considering demand response costs, green certificate costs and system operating costs are established, the constraints on the grid, heat network and devices are established. Finally, a comparative simulation of the two scenarios is established, and the simulation results show that the model proposed can effectively improve the level of new energy consumption while ensuring the economy of system operation in this paper.

articleTitle: Monitoring method for abnormal conditions of cement pre-decomposition based on PCA and MA-OCSVM algorithm
abstract: The stable operation of the rotary kiln system is affected by the operation state of cement pre-decomposition. So it is important to accurately monitor the operation state of cement pre-decomposition. In this paper, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and the One Class Support Vector Machine algorithm optimized by Mayfly Algorithm (MA-OCSVM) are proposed to monitor cement clinker pre-decomposition conditions. Firstly, the PCA algorithm is used to reduce the feature dimension of historical production data. Then a monitoring model of cement pre-decomposition conditions based on OCSVM is established, and the key parameters are optimized by MA method. When new operating data appears, it can be monitored by bringing it into the trained OCSVM model. Finally, 400 sets of online running data are selected to verify the method in this paper. The results show that the monitoring method of cement pre-decomposition condition based on PCA and MA-OCSVM algorithm has high monitoring effect. It provides a feasible method for monitoring the operation state of cement clinker pre-decomposition.

articleTitle: Uncalibrated visual servo algorithm based on RBF neural network optimizing maximum correntropy Kalman filter
abstract: A radial basis function neural network (RBF) modified maximum correntropy Kalman filter algorithm (RBFMCKF algorithm) is proposed for robot uncalibrated visual servo positioning control. Because there may be non-Gaussian measurement noise in robot visual servo, the maximum correntropy criterion (MCC) is introduced into KF framework to suppress the impact of non-Gaussian noise on filtering accuracy, and then RBF neural network is used to adjusting the error produced by the maximum correntropy Kalman filter (MCKF) algorithm. The simulation results show that the proposed RBFMCKF is effective and can effectively suppress the influence of non Gaussian noise on the filtering accuracy. It provides an idea for further optimizing the robot’s uncalibrated visual servo positioning control.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling of Microgrid Based on Improved Swarm Spider Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Microgrids have an important position in the smart grid, therefore, not only the stability of the microgrid should be considered, but also the economic efficiency and environmental protection of the microgrid should be improved. For this, a multi-objective optimization model that integrates the operating cost and environmental protection cost of the system under the grid-connected mode of microgrid is proposed. The revised swarm spider optimization algorithm is adopted for solving the model. The results indicate that this method can effectively decrease the cost of power consumption and environmental pollution on the customer side. Finally, the superior performance of the improved swarm spider optimization algorithm is verified when compared with the traditional swarm spider optimization algorithm algorithm.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field-oriented Control of Induction Reaction Sphere with Aerostatic-bearing Prototype
abstract: This paper proposes an induction reaction sphere aerostatic-bearing prototype, and designs a magnetic field-oriented control (FOC) model with torque control and flux linkage closed loop. The aerostatic-bearing prototype can be used for decoupling control of the rotation and suspension functions of the reaction sphere. The magnetic field-oriented control model can significantly improve the dynamic response performance of the controlled object. The three-phase current of the reaction sphere can be equivalent to the two-phase rotating coordinate system by using the rotor flux linkage orientation. So as to realize the decoupling control. The model can control the torque independently, which is beneficial to improve the decoupling performance of the closed-loop control system of rotational speed and flux linkage. Finally, the simulation of the designed vector control system is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the magnetic field-oriented control (FOC) model.

articleTitle: Grid-connected Inverter robust fault observation and identification in closed loop
abstract: This paper studies the design of the robust fault observer and identifier for closed loop grid-connected inverter. First, the closed loop grid-connected inverter system is mathematically modeled. Then the fault model of the system is analyzed. Thirdly, the fault observer is designed by solving linear matrix inequalities, which has good robustness. By choosing a suitable adaptive law, fault identifiers are designed for different circuit fault components. After the fault observer observes the circuit fault, the fault identifier can identify the specific location of the faulty component in the circuit. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed fault observer and identifier are verified by Simulink.

articleTitle: A Path Planning Method Based on Collaborative Learning for Multi-Robot with Connectivity and Obstacle Avoidance Constraints
abstract: Cooperative path planning method is one of the research hotspots in the field of multi-agent. In this paper, we study the problem of cooperative path planning, in which the robots under the constraints of communication connectivity and collision avoidance, and choose the destination location independently. It is difficult to find the optimal solution efficiently in sparse solution space by large-scale complex environments. To overcome the problem, in this paper, a novel collaborative learning algorithm, named Park Algorithm (PA) is proposed, which makes full use of exploration experience to improve the exploration efficiency. First, an objective function with three goals including path length, communication and collision is designed. Second, Marker Matrix is designed to evaluate the exploration value of the grids in the map, and each robot uses its own and teammates’ historical experience to update Marker Matrix. Our method can make full use of the exploration experience, realize self-learning and mutual learning between the robots, accelerate the exploration of solution space and avoid falling into local optimal solutions. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are verified by simulation analysis. The results show that our method has a better performance compared with Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm (PSO) and Ant Colony Algorithm (ACO).

articleTitle: An Accelerated Variance Reduction Stochastic ADMM for Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization
abstract: The variance reduction technique-based Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) has attracted a lot of attention due to its simplicity and practicability to provide an acceleration characteristic of various machine learning models. Most stochastic ADMM-type methods focus on convex models, however, it is not clear whether accelerated SVRG-ADMM (ASVRG-ADMM) for solving widely used nonconvex models has a similar acceleration feature or convergence rate as in the convex setting. To fill this gap, we consider a general nonconvex nonsmooth optimization problem and study the convergence of ASVRG-ADMM with momentum acceleration. By using a well-defined potential energy function, we establish its sublinear convergence rate. A number of experiments validate that the proposed ASVRG-ADMM performs better than some state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Backstepping-based Tracking Control for a Coaxial Rotor UAV
abstract: This paper takes a coaxial rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) as the research object, the problem of controlling the position and orientation of this UAV is solved. The nonlinear mathematical model of the coaxial rotor UAV is novelty present and a hierarchical controller is adopted to solve this problem. The controller includes the attitude controller of inner loop and the position controller of outer loop, which are both adopting backstepping control technique to track the reference position. Numerical simulations present that the coaxial rotor UAV can perfectly track the predefined trajectory, which demonstrates the good performance of the designed control strategy.

articleTitle: Voltage control strategy of high-penetration photovoltaic distribution network based on cluster division
abstract: The penetration rate of renewable energy in distribution network is getting higher and higher, and the access of distributed photovoltaic brings challenges to the dispatching and control of power system. This paper mainly studies the voltage control problem of distributed photovoltaic distribution network with high permeability. First, select the appropriate cluster division index to improve the modular increment, and apply Fast Newman algorithm to divide the distribution network into several clusters. On the basis of the cluster, a voltage autonomy strategy within the population is proposed. Reactive power is optimally allocated according to the voltage amplitude and network loss, and an improved serpentine optimization algorithm is proposed to solve the problem. Finally, the IEEE 33 bus standard system is taken as an example to verify the effectiveness of clustering and voltage control strategies.

articleTitle: Attack detection and defense of linear time-invariant systems with disturbances observer
abstract: In this paper, the problem of attack detection and defense for linear time-invariant systems with disturbances is studied. Unlike existing attack detection mechanisms, a new attack detection mechanism under disturbances is designed by output errors, whose trigger can be determined as attacks rather than disturbances. To solve the unobservable problem of the system under attacks, an augmented system and its auxiliary outputs are constructed until the observer matching condition is satisfied. Using estimates of augmented system states and unknown inputs, a state feedback controller is designed to defend against network attacks and ensure system stability. Theoretical analysis and simulation results verify the feasibility of the scheme.

articleTitle: A Faster Discrete-Time Tracking Differentiator and Its Numerical Simulation
abstract: In this paper, a faster tracking differentiator (TD) based on discrete time optimal control (DTOC) is presented. Based on base transformation, the algorithm is simplified. The problems of curve approximation and complexity of the calculation are successfully solved together. The numerical simulation shows that the the convergence of the tracking differentiator and better performance to solve the problem of the complexity of the calculation.

articleTitle: Actuator and sensor fault tolerant control for Steer-by-Wire systems: Recent Advances
abstract: Steer-by-Wire (SBW) system is considered one of the most important steering approaches and has a great impact on driving safety and vehicle stability. To meet the safety requirement, the SBW system is supposed to tolerate critical faults and maintain proper steering performance. This paper summarizes some of the major advancements in fault tolerant control (FTC) strategies for actuator and sensor faults during the previous few years. We also discuss the current fault detection and isolation tools and present the challenges to FTC for the SBW system and provide potential future research areas.

articleTitle: Adaptive NN Formation Control for Autonomous Vehicles with Uncertain Dynamics
abstract: In this brief, we discuss the formation control of autonomous vehicles. The formation structure uses a leader follower strategy. The vehicles have underactuated characteristics and unknown dynamics. Neural network (NN) is used to approximate the unknown nonlinear function, and the model of uncertain system is established. Meanwhile, the command filtering technique is applied to avoid the problem of burst intricacy intrinsic in the backstepping procedure. Only internal sensors are used to measure and control the line-of-sight range and angle, and no additional instructions about leaders are required; besides, the NN formation controller developed can capture and approximate the unknown dynamics of the vehicle, which reduces the requirement for the accuracy of the vehicle dynamics model. The NN system can also capture and approximate the nonlinear terms of the vehicle, such as wind resistance and friction. The stability of the controller is proved by Lyapunov function. The semi global uniform limit boundedness of the closed loop signal is also guaranteed. Simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Koopman Autoencoder Predicting Nonlinear System States: Effect of Latent Layer Neuron Number
abstract: Researchers have always been popular with analyzing and controlling nonlinear systems, yet most methods are based on local linearized models. As an alternative, Koopman theory was introduced to solve global linearization problems. Koopman operator is infinite-dimensional and has the ability to globally linearize nonlinear systems without information loss. In this work, a Koopman autoencoder, which combines the Koopman operator and autoencoder network, is used for predicting nonlinear systems. The autoencoder network is designed to find an approximate finite-dimensional Koopman operator. An inverted pendulum dynamic system is used to evaluate the effectiveness of the Koopman autoencoder, and accurate prediction results have been achieved. Furthermore, we discussed the effect of latent layer neuron number in the Koopman autoencoder, prediction results are given, and the best number of latent layer neurons for this system is found.

articleTitle: Radar Object Detection Based on Multi-scale Spatiotemporal Features Fusion and Attention Network
abstract: Radar signals can describe the environment more reliably than RGB images when the light is too strong or too weak or the object is occluded. Radar frequency (RF) images are common representation of radar signals and contain rich motion information, but are not as intuitive data as RGB images. Effectively utilizing radar semantic information is a challenge in radar object detection task. In our work, we focus on the extraction of RF images semantic information, and propose a feature extraction network named multi-scale spatiotemporal features fusion and attention network (MSFFANet). An Encoder-Decoder framework with skip connections is used to realize the end-to-end radar object detection. Firstly, in order to effectively utilize the motion information in radar signals, a multi-scale spatiotemporal features fusion block (MSFFB) is designed. Standard 3D convolution and 3D dilated convolution are both used to process the input RF image sequences to achieve cross-channel multi-scale features fusion. Secondly, in order to focus more on the features of the object in the decoder network, the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) is beneficial to weight the features, strengthen the useful features and achieve feature refinement. Finally, experiments and evaluations are performed on the ROD2021 dataset. The average precision rate reaches 76.5542%, the average recall rate reaches 80.4734% and the F1-Score is 0.7846. Compared with the best performance in radar object detection network (RODNet) [4], our method improves 1.6117% in average precision rate, 1.432% in average recall rate and 0.0152 in F1-Score.

articleTitle: Research on Generator Test Data Processing and Fault Diagnosis
abstract: In order to improve the automation of the generator test system, this paper proposes a Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) signal processing method combined with an Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm and Support Vector Machine (IWOA-SVM) pattern recognition method to process test data and diagnose generator faults. VMD processes current signals to obtain several Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) and extracts the energy entropy as feature vectors. Then, aiming at the shortcoming of WOA's insufficient global search ability, an improved WOA is proposed by introducing adaptive weight and a variable spiral position update strategy. IWOA is used to optimize SVM parameters to improve classification accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed method can accurately extract the fault information and improve the accuracy of fault identification. The diagnostic accuracy based on the actual generator test data is 93.75%, which proves that the method is feasible.

articleTitle: A Study of Path Planning for Multi- UAVs in Random Obstacle Environment Based on Improved Artificial Potential Field Method
abstract: In this paper, an improved artificial potential field method is proposed and studied for path planning and obstacle avoidance of multi-UAVs. Based on the traditional artificial potential field method, a dynamic attraction factor and a dynamic repulsion factor are introduced to improve the potential field function and solve the problems of excessive attractive force, path optimization and safety in the obstacle avoidance process, and are applied to multi-UAV path planning. MATLAB simulation is used to demonstrate the feasibility of the improved algorithm in multi-UAV path planning.

articleTitle: Model-Free Fault-Tolerant Control of Feedback Linearizable Systems Under Multiple Faults
abstract: The fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem for a class of feedback linearizable systems under severe model uncertainties, process faults, sensor faults, and actuator faults is explored in this paper. This causes the system dynamics both unknown and time-varying, which fails to be addressed by identification, approximation or diagnosis, straightforward. To solve this problem, a novel model-free FTC approach is put forward, which is just a static error feedback by a combination of a transformation function, a barrier function and an orientation function. Therefore, the controller exhibits significant simplicity. Instead of the classical Lyapunov stability analysis, a constraint analysis based on dialectic by contradiction is conducted, which reveals the robustness of the resulting control system against the unknown nonlinear dynamics and the system faults. Finally, simulation studies are carried out to clarify and verify the effectiveness and the superiority of our approach.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Fault Estimation Observer Design for Head-Two-Arms-Trunk System
abstract: This paper presents a observer-based fault estimation strategy for patients with complete spinal cord injury (SCI) that modeled by nonlinear Head-Two-Arms-Trunk (H2AT) system. Due to the complexity of nonlinear H2AT system structure, a Takagi-Sugeno (TS) fuzzy m odel technique is adopted to facility the observer design. However, an undesired unmeasured premise variables are raised which leads to well-known difficulty in designing TS fuzzy observer. To this end, a special fuzzy modeling method named N-TS model is proposed in this paper where the unmeasured nonlinearities are isolated in the local nonlinear consequent. With this model, unmeasurable nonlinear terms are avoid. Moreover, the complexity of the observer structure is reduced which is suit for the practical application. The conditions of designing observer-based fault estimation strategy are given in term of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) which can be efficiently solved by the existing numerical toolbox. Simulation results presents the effectiveness of the proposed fault estimation method.

articleTitle: Model-Based Event-Triggered Adaptive Tracking Control for Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems Under DoS Attacks
abstract: The manuscript highlights on a model-based event-triggered (ET) adaptive tracking control problem for uncertain discrete-time (DT) non-linear systems when denial of service (DoS) attacks exist in the communication network. To deal with this matter, this work firstly suggests a new and original dynamic ET mechanism to control the frequency of data transmission. Subsequently, using the approximation ability of highorder nonlinear neural network, a switching estimation model is constructed to resist the adverse effects of signal loss caused by DoS attacks. Then, a model-based neural network controller is derived. Through iterative techniques and Lyapunov’s theorem, the ultimately uniformly boundedness of the estimation error of the estimation model and the stability of the closed-loop system will be strongly demonstrated. The usefulness and effectiveness of the suggested approach are confirmed by a simulation study.

articleTitle: Efficient Video Stitching for an Eagle-Eye-Based Vision System
abstract: Computer vision has always been one of the research hotspots in the field of artificial intelligence. Inspired by the characteristics of eagle eye, this paper first designs a bionic visual imaging module that contains two wide-angle cameras and one telephoto camera. Then, video stitching and video fusion are accomplished by exploring the fact that relative poses of these three cameras keep constant. Results of extensive experiments show that the eagle-eye-based vision system can acquire large field of view and local high-resolution images simultaneously, which lays a good foundation for subsequent vision tasks.

articleTitle: Modeling and Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Vibration Control of the Flexible Wing with End Loads
abstract: An innovative three-dimensional model of flexible wing is built, which is counted as a distributed parameter system. For the parameter uncertainty and unknown actuator fault of this system, an adaptive fault-tolerant control method combined with boundary control is designed to maintain stability. By using the Lyapunov-based method, the uniform boundedness is theoretically proved in this closed-loop system. The efficacy and feasibility of the strategy can be demonstrated by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Distributed Leader-Following Impulsive Consensus of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Partial Input Saturation
abstract: In this letter, leader-following consensus of a nonlinear MASs satisfying Lipschitz conditions with partial actuator saturation constraints is investigated First of all, an impulse control protocol which only requires local information of agents and their neighbors is proposed. Then, using Lyapunov stability theory, impulse control theory, and algebraic graph theory, sufficient conditions for the consensus of multi-agent systems are provided. Ultimately, numerical simulations are employed to show that the research findings are accurate.

articleTitle: A model-free approach to approximate the solution of time-varying optimal control based on Bezier control points technique
abstract: Aiming at the unsatisfactory effect of conventional control methods on time-varying control systems with unknown models, this paper proposes an on-line finite-time adaptive optimal control algorithm based on a data-driven model. More precisely, the realization of the algorithm relies on the on-policy adaptive dynamic programming and Bezier control point methods, where the Bezier curve is used to approximate the optimal control solution (i.e., the solution of the time-varying differential Riccati equation corresponding to the finite-time optimal control) and the on-policy adaptive dynamic programming is performed in the form of on-line iterative process to approximate successively the solution of the control strategy. At last, a simulation example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Correlation Filtering Object Tracking Algorithm Based on Motion Estimation
abstract: In order to solve the bounding box deviation while the object moves rapidly, which will cause the loss of the object, an improved Kernelized Correlation Filter object tracking algorithm is proposed based on motion estimation. The block-matching algorithm is used to estimate the motion of the tracking object in the adjacent frames of the video sequence, and the estimated results are quantified to judge the severity of the object’s motion. Then the size of the search box is adaptively adjusted. Two data sets of both OTB100 and OTB50 are selected for the experiments. The experimental results show that the improved algorithm can effectively solve the problem of object loss caused by rapid object movement and achieve long-term stable tracking of objects.

articleTitle: Multi-layer Convolution Transform Learning Algorithm based on Manifold Optimization Method
abstract: Convolutional transform learning (CTL) is a combination of convolutional neural networks and transform learning, which learns convolutional kernels by minimizing loss functions in an unsupervised way, is gaining widespread attention. However, the traditional methods usually learn convolution kernels first in Euclidean space and then an additional operations are required to meet the orthonormal constraints to avoid trivial solutions. To solve this problem, we propose a multi-layer CTL model based on manifold optimization. The manifold optimization method can calculate and update the convolution kernel group directly and effectively on the manifold constructed with the orthonormality constraint, which achieve the representation of important inherent properties of data. In addition, we extend the single-layer CTL model based on manifold optimization to multi-layer CTL model, which can extract the deep semantic information of signals. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can reduce the number of iteration updates of the convolution kernel and improve the sparse feature extraction ability of the convolution kernel, and thus extract higher quality sparse features.

articleTitle: Decision probability transformation based on prospect theory
abstract: In the decision-making process, transforming the mass function into the decision probability can remove the uncertainty of knowledge and thus reduce the difficulty of decision making. For this reason, this paper puts forward a novel transformation approach based on the value function of prospect theory. The new approach considers the support degree of the single subset from the perspective of uncertainty interval on the basis of the value function of prospect theory. Then, we can get the allocation ratio according to significance of single subsets, which is used to allocate distribute the mass of multiple subsets. The new approach proposed in this paper satisfies the two properties of probability transformation. Furthermore, the performance of the new approach is evaluated by the corresponding evaluation criteria. In the end, the rationality of the new method is well illustrated by several examples.

articleTitle: Agile Earth Observation Satellite Mission Planning Based on Adaptive Gaussian Mutation Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Compared with integer coding, real number coding can iteratively optimize the observation time of the target in agile Earth satellite mission planning. However, because the real number solution space is huge, and the mutation operator rarely considers the mutation step, the existing genetic algorithm cannot well balance the global and local search capabilities. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes an adaptive Gaussian mutation genetic algorithm (AGMGA). Firstly, according to the satellite constraints, a fitness function is established that considers the target observation revenue and the energy consumption of satellite attitude maneuvers. Secondly, the discrete solution space of task selection and the continuous solution space of task observation time are coupled by using the real number coding rule based on relative imaging time. Then, in the genetic algorithm, the adaptive mutation operator and the Gaussian mutation operator are combined to optimize the mutation probability and the mutation step at the same time. Finally, through comparative simulation, it is verified that AHMGA has better optimization effect in different scales of task planning.

articleTitle: City-level Charging Demand Forecast Based on Shared Electric Vehicle Usage Behavior
abstract: The current city-level electric vehicle (EV) charging system lacks data support. Driven by this motivation, this paper puts forward a city-level charging demand prediction model in view of the behavior of shared EVs. First, a three-network coupling model of “transportation network-charging station-distribution network” is proposed, and then the original travel trajectory data of real EVs is used for data mining, through spatial grid modeling, trajectory data mapping, urban functional area clustering, etc. The method obtains feature data information such functional region division as EV travel regularity distribution, establishing a single EV model including EV classification, driving characteristics and charging characteristics, and then uses the tackling data attained by modeling analysis and the homogeneous EV model as the data sources and model support for charging demand forecasting framework. Finally, citing a specific zone in Chongqing as a case, the simulation analysis is carried out. Final results show that the claimed model can anticipate predict the spatiotemporal distribution feature of the charging demand load on three date types and various functional region effectively, laying a solid theoretical ground-work for controlling and guiding.

articleTitle: Safety Analysis of Train-Ground Communication Failure Based on Unfolding of Petri Nets
abstract: With the continuous development of train control technology, the research of the next generation train control (NGTC) becomes increasingly important. The NGTC system is complex and safety-critical, so the safety of the system is essential. This paper focuses on the train-ground communication failure of the NGTC system and proposes a new method based on the unfolding of Petri nets and path searching. By unfolding the complex Petri net and directly finding the path that leads to the occurrence of the hazardous state. The cause of the hazard due to train-ground communication failure can be found successfully.

articleTitle: Adaptive Model Predictive Control for AGVs Based on Disturbance Observers
abstract: This paper studies the robust trajectory tracking problem for AGVs based on model predictive control strategy, where an extended state observer is developed to estimate the external disturbance. A robust adaptive minimum invariant set is proposed according to the estimation of disturbances, based on which some conservatism is reduced compared with existing common methods. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the method.
