articleTitle: A Multimodal EEG Identification Method for Complex Aerospace Target Recognition
abstract: Accurate recognition of aerospace targets in complex flight scenarios is the primary crucial link to achieve intelligent decision-making and control of aircraft. In the face of open complex flight environments with variants, camouflage and deception, traditional target recognition methods cannot meet the needs of practical applications, and the performance of computer automatic image analysis methods is far from human recognition ability. This paper innovatively proposes a complex aerospace target recognition method based on multimodal EEG identification: proposes EEG signal acquisition and pre-processing techniques under complex visual stimulation, and accurately obtains EEG representation information under relevant visual stimulation; design a multi-wavelet analysis-based time-frequency feature extraction method and multi-scale time-domain feature extraction technology, and obtain effective discriminatory EEG features under different stimulation. The method is designed to obtain multimodal EEG features with effective discriminative ability under different stimuli. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively identify the target of interest, which is of great significant for promoting the development of intelligent perception and recognition models for new generation unmanned systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Fixed-time Tracking Control of Underactuated USVs With External Disturbances
abstract: This paper focuses on the fixed-time tracking control of underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) with environmental disturbances. An adaptive neural fixed-time control (ANFTC) scheme is proposed for tracking control of underactuated USVs. Neural network is introduced to approximate the unknown dynamics and external disturbances of USVs. Theoretical analysis proves that under the proposed control scheme, the controlled system can achieve the practical fixed-time stability and the tracking errors of the USV will converge to small neighbourhood of zero in fixed time independent on initial conditions. Finally, numerical simulations are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed control strategy.

articleTitle: Sequential fusion state estimation algorithm for multi-sensor nonlinear systems with cross-correlated noise
abstract: This paper is concerned the problem of multi-sensor state estimation with cross-correlated noise, this paper adopts sequential fusion to estimate the state. The statistical characteristics of measurement noise of different sensors in the multi-sensor system is related, and also related to the system noise in one step. Firstly, based on the estimation of observation noise, a global optimal fusion filter based on sequential fusion and Cubature Kalman filter is proposed for the first time. Secondly, the algorithm proposed in this paper is simulated by numerical method. The method of numerical realization is Cubature Kalman filter based on deterministic sampling. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Wind Disturbance Estimation and Compensation for Quadcopters using Fuzzy Neural Network
abstract: In this paper, the fuzzy neural network (FNN) with reinforced rules is used to estimate the wind disturbance of quadcopters in real time, and the wind disturbance compensation is performed on the position loop, attitude loop, and lift loop according to the estimated disturbance. Among them, the neural network part is used for data-driven modeling of complex aerodynamic effects of quadcopters, the fuzzy part is used to improve the interpretability of the conventional neural network, and the reinforced rules are used for improving the generalization ability of conventional FNN to quadcopters whose computational resources are limited. Simulation and comparative studies have been conducted to verify the effectiveness and merits of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Robust Estimation for Hammerstein Models Based on Variational Inference
abstract: The paper presents a robust identification method using variational inference (VI) for Hammerstein models in the presence of process noise and non-Gaussian colored measurement noise. First of all the measurements and process output are described as Student’s t and Gaussian distribution by using introduced variational parameters. Then the conjugate prior information of introduced parameters is framed for sake of a closed-loop solution. By applying the idea of VI, estimates of system parameters are got by minimizing Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. Finally, a numerical simulation example is used to show the effectiveness of the proposed identification method compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Finite-Time Control for Nonstrict Feedback Stochastic Systems with Prescribed Performance
abstract: In this research, tracking error-constrained control programs for a class of stochastic nonlinear systems with non-strict feedback is studied in finite time. By utilizing the error transfer function, a controller is developed by recursive design and adaptive neural network control to meet the prescribed performance control scheme. Based on the stochastic finite-time stability theory, the closed-loop signals can be realized to be semi-globally finite-time stable in probability(SGFSP). Finally, a simulation example displays the availability of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Optimal Combination Scheduling of Drone Based on Forest Fire Ignition Point Data
abstract: Forest fires have occurred from time to time, each time accompanied by huge loss of public property and even threatening human life. In order to solve this problem, drones can be used to replace part of the manual monitoring work. To make drone monitoring more scientific, the importance of different areas is divided by analyzing the forest fire point data over the years. Through the meshing of the target area, the entire data is coordinated and planned to bring the model closer to reality. Then drones group deployment model based on the imperialist competition algorithm is established, and the model can effectively reduce costs and improve efficiency through simulation verification. Finally, considering the influence of altitude on UAV communication, a new positioning model is proposed, and the Imperialist Competition Algorithm is used to optimize the coordinates of the relay station. Simulation results show that the model can effectively reduce costs and improve efficiency.

articleTitle: Dynamic Data Reconciliation for Improving the Model Prediction Results based on Just-in-time Kernel Learning
abstract: Many process variables in chemical production have distributed characteristics, and traditional hardware and offline measurements to monitor these distributed variables cannot meet the requirements of modern production. As an alternative to hardware measurements, soft sensors are increasingly used in the process industries. In order to realize online monitoring of distributed process outputs, a soft sensor model based on just-in-time kernel learning (JKL) is developed in this paper. Furthermore, for the prediction error of the model, dynamic data reconciliation (DDR) is proposed to improve the prediction results of the JKL model. DDR integrates inaccurate measurement information and model prediction information, and uses the Bayesian formula to obtain the optimal estimated outputs. Finally, DDR is used to improve the molecular weight distribution (MWD) prediction results in polymerization processes to verify its effectiveness. The results show that the proposed method can further improve the accuracy of the predicted outputs of the JKL models.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic transceiver circuit design
abstract: This paper proposes an ultrasonic transmitting and receiving circuit system based on DYSTM32F4 high-frequency ultrasonic development board, which is used in the research of drilling ultrasonic logging instrument (ULISSD). First of all, we introduce the DYSTM32F4 high-frequency ultrasonic development board, and then analyze the principle of ultrasonic transmitting and receiving from the circuit composition, at last, through experiments to verify the circuit system waveform, used for the whole design system test. Combined with the test results, it is evaluated that this system can achieve the function of ultrasonic wave transmitting and receiving.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Predictive Control for Networked Control System under DoS Attack
abstract: In this paper, the control strategy for the disturbed network control system (NCS) under two-channel denial-of-service (DoS) attack is designed. To defend two-channel DoS attacks, an event-triggered control predictive control strategy is presented to make sure that the inputs are able to be compensated. Under the consideration of disturbance, a controller ensuring the system states converge to an invariant set is designed. Meanwhile, a sufficient condition is obtained to guarantee the uniformly ultimate boundness of the closed-loop system. Numerical examples are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the developed approach.

articleTitle: A Diabetes Risk Assessment Model Using Limited Vitro Physiological Indicators
abstract: A majority of reported diabetes assessment models using physiological indicators as input features use vitro physiological indicators such as blood glucose, insulin, which are difficult to measure and unobtained in daily life, leading to low practicality of reported models. To overcome this issue, this paper proposed a diabetes risk assessment model using limited vitro physiological indicators, which can be measured and obtained easily. This model provided advice about diabetes risk based on the values of input physiological indicators, in this way alerting people at high diabetes risk to prevent diabetes in early stages. Feature-weighted k-Nearest Neighbors (FW-kNN) algorithm was used to build the model, manta ray foraging optimization (MRFO) algorithm was used for searching the optimal feature weights, 10-fold cross-validation and 4:1 training-testing method were adapted to evaluate the performance of the proposed FW-kNN algorithm. The results of experiments revealed that the proposed FW-kNN algorithm achieved 70.9% accuracy using 10-fold cross-validation and the area under receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) was 0.80, which proved the proposed FW-kNN algorithm had a good performance and the outputs of the proposed FW- kNN model were of reference to diabetes risk assessment.

articleTitle: Time Series Production Simulation for Renewable Energy Consumption Considering Section Constraints
abstract: As high-quality clean energy, wind power and photovoltaic power can markedly diminish the expenditure of electricity generation. However, as ample wind power and photovoltaics has been connected to the grid, their uncertainty has brought momentous "wind abandonment" and "photovoltaic abandonment" phenomena to the power system. In this paper, the power characteristics of wind power, photovoltaic power, thermal power, hydroelectric power, pumped storage, and battery storage are fully considered to model the multi-energy power system. Considering the system section constraints, the time-series production simulation method is used to evaluate the renewable energy consumption capacity. And it studied the impact of renewable energy installed capacity, energy storage capacity, and the configuration of energy storage on the accommodation capacity.

articleTitle: Patch Elastic Deformation: An Effective Data Augmentation Method
abstract: In image detection, various models and data enhancement algorithms have emerged in recent years. But these methods are either random copy-paste or rotation but seldom consider the local deformation caused by the partial extrusion of the object. Elastic deformation exists widely in the real world. Patch Elastic Deformation simulates the shape changes of things after various reality effects. As a complement to existing data augmentation methods, elastic deformation may appear anywhere in the sample, increasing the richness of the selection. Specifically, we randomly select a rectangle patch in the image and then apply elastic deformation to it, forcing models to extract input images’ essential features. For image classification and object detection tasks, we verify the effectiveness of our algorithm on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and PASCAL VOC datasets. And we also compared it with the random erasing algorithm, proving that our algorithm can boost the performance of models.

articleTitle: Robust Stability and Stabilization of Incommensurate Fractional-Order Uncertain Systems: A Parameter Space Method
abstract: This paper discusses the robust stability and stabilization of incommensurate fractional-order uncertain systems by the parameter space method. Analyzing the Jacobian matrix around the equilibrium points is a direct way to test whether systems satisfy the asymptotic stability theorem. The asymptotic stability theorem of incommensurate fractional-order systems is an expansion of the commensurate ones. This expansion often makes the characteristic equation of the Jacobian matrix high-dimensional. When systems are with uncertain parameters, it is difficult to solve all roots of the high-dimensional equation. In this paper, a parameter space method is proposed by transforming the high-dimensional characteristic equation into a parameter-dependent equation, for selecting the complete stable region from the parameter space directly. One example shows robust stability and stabilization results by using the parameter space method.

articleTitle: Implementation of an Interactive Panoramic Course Learning Platform
abstract: Most of the current online teaching platforms use ordinary monocular cameras to capture teaching courses, and many teaching videos just record the offline teaching process and then put them on the online platform. This kind of teaching course is not immersive enough, students cannot get a sense of presence when learning through the online platform, and they cannot get answers in time when they have questions, which will affect the students' learning effect. Compared with the video collected by the ordinary camera, the panoramic video obtained from the panoramic camera has a wider field of view and a better sense of presence and immersion. Our system uses panoramic cameras to collect on-site teaching videos to form 360-degree viewable course videos and upload them to the server for storage. At the same time, a question-and-answer dialogue-assisted teaching robot that can interact with voice is constructed through a server-side dialogue Q&A module. The client is used to display the interactive interface of panoramic video courses and dialog with the question-answering robot teaching assistants. Students can consult the "robot assistant" if they have any questions when watching the course videos through the client. This creates an "immersive" learning atmosphere and avoids repetitive work by the instructor while achieving better learning results.

articleTitle: A functional data feature learning method with EM algorithm in industrial soft sensing modeling
abstract: Functional principal component analysis (FPCA) is an effective model to establish a connection for each discrete variable by functional modeling in industrial process plants. However, process variables usually contain perturbations by random noise. In order to extend the capabilities of FPCA in handling process noise, the functional probabilistic principal component analysis (FPPCA) is introduced in this paper. Firstly, process variables are transformed into functional data through basis function modeling. Subsequently, a log-likelihood function involved in functional data is designed, and the regression model parameters can then be estimated through the expectation maximization (EM) algorithm, iteratively. Applications of a numerical case and the Tennessee Eastman (TE) process are exploited to demonstrate the performance of FPPCA.

articleTitle: The Design of Distributed Calibration Algorithm and Its Application to MEMS Inertial Sensors
abstract: Micro-Electro-Mechanical System (MEMS) can be mass-produced, which integrates the micro sensor, micro actuator and control circuit, interfaces, and communication. MEMS inertial devices have the characteristics of small, lightweight, low cost, and homogeneity. How to improve the accuracy or reduce the cost is the engineering requirement. Considering the homogeneity of the MEMS sensors, the batch calibration method is one of the feasible ways to reduce cost. This paper proposes the distributed calibration method which is different from the traditional system-level and discrete calibration. The distributed calibration method requires only one or a few rotations of the combined and arranged devices to excite the individual error parameters of the inertial instruments. The relationship between the error parameters and the navigation error is rewritten via equivalence transformation. The 24 error parameters of the sensor are identified by the distributed least-squares estimation method using the velocity error as the observed quantity. Through simulation experiments, the method can calibrate more MEMS devices simultaneously than the traditional calibration method with the same accuracy requirement.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Control Method for Uncertain Teleoperation Systems with Time-Varying Delays and Disturbance
abstract: In this paper, a non-singular terminal sliding surface method which includes arctan function (ANTSM) and mixed-type errors is proposed for the serious effects of internal uncertainties and unknown additional disturbance on the stability as well as the control performance of teleoperation systems. The suggested sliding surface’s finite temporal stability is ensured through stability analysis. In addition, the compensation bound for online estimation is proposed to cope with the performance degradation caused by time-varying delays introduced by communication channel. To improve the transparency of the master, force prediction is combined with RBF neural-network (RBFNN) to reconstruct the environmental force with unknown impedance structure, avoiding the direct transmission of force signals. Finally, dual three degrees of freedom (3 DOFs) manipulators based on geomagic touch models are used to verify the validity of designed controllers.

articleTitle: An Improved U-Net Model for Astronomical Images Denoising
abstract: To explore and understand the universe, it is inevitable to analyze astronomical images. But additional and incidental noise information will be added during the acquisition process. These noise will interfere with the sub-sequent image analysis. Hence it is necessary to denoise the astronomical images before analyzing. Astronomical image resolution is large and the star signal is small. Meanwhile,the existing denoising methods are difficult to recover the feature information of stars. To enhance the ability of detail feature extraction while denoising, we propose an improved U-Net model. First, we add the residual connections inside the network to break the symmetry of the network. Residual connections are useful to information transmission, and avoid gradient explosion and overfitting. Meanwhile, residual connections can improve the network representation ability. Secondly, we use the encoding and decoding parts of Receptive Field Block(RFB) connection model. RFB increases the receptive field to strengthen the capability of multi-scale fea-ture extraction. RFB also recover more feature information of stars. Finally, we used an improved upsampling method to avoid generating checkerboard pattern of artifacts. We use the dataset from the Hubble Space Telescope(HST) Archives to verify the experiment. The experimental results verify that the proposed model performs well in the task of astronomical image denoising. Our method can better remove the existing noise of astronomical images and recover the feature in-formation of stars.

articleTitle: State-of-Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Battery Based on Multi-Segment Fusion
abstract: The state-of-health (SOH) estimation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for the safe operation, intelligent maintenance, and life prediction of electric vehicles (EVs). Due to the complex operation conditions of EVs, such as the random depth-of-discharge cycling, incomplete or seldom full charging, accurate SOH estimation is still challenging in real application. In this paper, a novel SOH estimation method based on multiple small charging segments is proposed to achieve flexibility and high accuracy at the same time. With this method, any one of the small segments can be used to estimate SOH for flexibility. The multiple segments can be fused to improve the estimation accuracy. The proposed method is validated by an open-source dataset, which indicates that the SOH can be estimated with less than 2.5% maximum percentage error by any one of the small charging segments, and less than 1.5% maximum percentage error by the fusion of multiple small charging segments.

articleTitle: Efficiency optimal control of PEMFC system considering thermal management
abstract: Thermal management of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is the key factor affecting its safe, stable and efficient operation. Firstly, a PEMFC nonlinear simulation model coupled with thermal management subsystem is built. The nonlinear model is linearized and a control- oriented linear model is obtained. Then, a control strategy based on offset-free explicit model predictive control (EMPC) is designed and verified by software in the loop (SiL) platform, which realized accurate and real-time power tracking besides efficiency optimization under system constraints.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning Method for Driverless Sweeper in Unstructured Environment
abstract: In the paper, we propose an approach for full coverage path planning and obstacle avoidance trajectory planning in the unstructured environment, applied to the driverless sweeper with Ackermann-like steering. The approach uses the boustrophedon cell decomposition method to solve the full-coverage path planning problem while using DWA (Dynamic Window Approach) and A* and a finite state machine to solve the planning problem of obstacle avoidance trajectories. A kinematics model of the Ackermann-like steering structure sweeper is established to make the obstacle avoidance trajectory satisfy the kinematic constraints. The method designs a corresponding trajectory evaluation function to make the DWA applicable to the sweeping scenario. And a finite state machine model is designed for the decision problem in obstacle avoidance. Finally, using a physical sweeper of 1.5m x 1.0m x 1.2m size in a factory environment verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of State Detection System Based on Big Data
abstract: With the development of technology, demands of safety operation get more and more higher. In order to avoid system failure and reduce the maintenance cost, applying state detection technology to monitor system’s operation state in real time becomes more and more important. A big data state detection method which based on multi-scale analysis was proposed. It can realize the operation monitoring of equipment. Besides, at the hardware level, edge computing platforms with different performance were designed, such as raspberry computing module, F1C100S and STM32F series, which could collect equipment operation data via 4G or 5G networks, compute operation status. At present, the condition monitoring platform runs stably and has achieved good results.

articleTitle: CMFST : Class-based Multi-scale Fusion Self-training for Adapting Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Learning domain-invariant representations has been adopted by mainstream approaches of unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) to alleviate the domain gap between source data with rich label and unlabeled target data. Self-training is a simple and popular method in UDA by training networks with target pseudo-labels. However, the pseudo-labels’ quality is limited by the single scale output of unadapted network, which has an important impact on training process. To address this issue, we propose a class-based multi-scale fusion (CMF) method that allows the unadapted network to achieve better prediction results by confirming class-scale relation and fusing specific classes prediction from appropriate scales. Our approach doesn’t rely on complex components, therefore is simple, efficient, and easy to transfer. We achieve competitive performance (measured by the Intersection-over-Union, IoU) in the GTA5 to Cityscapes and the SYNTHIA to Cityscapes scenarios which demonstrates the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Research of Gesture Recognition Based on Improved Convolutional Neural Network and Support Vector Machine
abstract: Aiming at the cumbersome feature extraction of gesture recognition, time-consuming network training, and low network recognition accuracy, an optimization algorithm based on improved convolutional neural network (CNN) and support vector machine (SVM) was proposed. The idea of multi-layer convolution in series is used to construct the neural network model, so as to obtain better ability of gesture feature extraction. Batch normalization (BN) layer is added after relu function to prevent over fitting. The fully connected layer is replaced by an adaptive global average pool (GAP) layer to reduce the network parameters. SVM classifier in machine learning is used to replace Softmax classifier, which improves the classification ability of the model. Through experimental verification, compared with the traditional CNN, the proposed model greatly improves the accuracy of gesture recognition and effectively shortens the convergence time of the model.

articleTitle: Research on Generalized Predictive Control of Hybrid Magnetic Bearing System
abstract: A generalized predictive control technique for hybrid magnetic bearings is put forth in this study. Firstly, a nonlinear model is established for the radial freedom of hybrid magnetic bearing, and is then linearized through small perturbation method at the equilibrium point, it is used to develop a generalized predictive controller. Then, the technique’s results proposed on the radial freedom floating control is analyzed together with the interference suppression ability, meanwhile the effect of main control parameters and the performance of the system are analyzed and compared, which contrast the conventional PID control approach. The simulation’s findings indicate that the generalized predictive control system presented has a better dynamic performance and robustness.

articleTitle: A Cooperative Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Dual Environment selection strategies
abstract: Constrained multi-objective optimization problems (CMOPs) involves both conflicting objective function and various constraints. Numerous constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (CMOEAs) have been proposed to deal with CMOPs. Accordingly, this paper adopts a co-evolutionary framework for constrained multi-objective optimization. The main population is responsible for the original constrained multi-objective optimization. The help population search the unconstrained derived from the original CMOP. Dual population coevolution is helpful to promote the convergence of the algorithm. To further improve the performance of the algorithm, this article proposes dual environment selection strategies. The two populations adopt different environment selection strategies to improve the diversity of the individuals. The proposed algorithm is compared with four advanced constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms on 24 bench-mark CMOPs. The experimental results demonstrate the competitiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Knowledge distillation and attention mechanism analysis of traffic sign detection
abstract: Safe driving has been the core of the traditional traffic, it is also a top priority for the future of autonomous driving. In recent years, with the development of target detection, a large number of proven technique have entered the realm of driverless cars. Traffic sign detection has always been an important task of pattern recognition in the traffic field. After the rise of deep learning, it quickly replaced the traditional methods and became the mainstream technology path. Object detection algorithms represented by RCNN family and YOLO series have gained extensive attention and applications. These algorithms are difficult to strike a good balance between speed and quality, especially when deployed on mobile platforms with less ability for calculate. In this paper, YOLOv5 algorithm is selected as the basis for knowledge distillation and multiple attention modes are used to improve the accuracy of the algorithm, and sparse training is used to further reduce the size of the model to achieve ultra-lightweight. The TT100K data set was used for training and verification results. However, the 45 types of traffic signs in this data set do not have the most important signal light data in traffic indication,ours made a large amount of such data to expand TT100K and named it as ETT100K data set.Experimental results show that the addition of attention to YOLOv5 can not effectively improve the model accuracy compared with knowledge distillation, but knowledge distillation can significantly improve the results.

articleTitle: CO2Det: Anchor-free based Convex-hull Generation Network for Oriented Object Detection
abstract: Nowadays, arbitrary oriented object detection has achieved considerable progress in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. However, there remains challenges of label assignment and loss discontinuity. To put the axe in the helve, we propose an anchor-free Convex-hull Oriented Object Detector (CO<sup>2</sup> Det). In CO<sup>2</sup>Det, the convex-hull feature expression(CFE) module and Kullback-Leibler Divergence(KLD) loss are proposed, based on the 135° long edge prediction box definition. In the CFE, a convex-hull set is constructed for each object so strengthen the connection of non-axis aligned feature from background pixels or adjacent objects. To maintain the loss continuity and scale invariance, a general rotation detection loss KLD is devised that transform the convex-hull parameters into a 2-D Gaussian distribution. KLD is applied to release mutual constraints between parameters so that adjust the direction optimization strategy adaptively. The DOTA and HRSC2016 public datasets are chosen to train our model and achieved the state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Backstepping Algorithms for Leader-Follower Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: The robust prescribed-time algorithms for nonlinear high-order systems and leader-follower systems are investigated with the help of backstepping approach. Firstly, for nonlinear high-order systems, the states can converge to zero within a prescribed time by designing virtual input in each step. Secondly, for leader-follower systems, new error function is defined to achieved consensus among followers and to ensure that follower’s states are identical to leader’s states within the prescribed time that has been arbitrarily set. In addition, the proposed algorithms all have disturbance rejection ability. To show that the suggested algorithms are effective, two numerical simulations are utilised in the end.

articleTitle: Driver Advisory System for Freight Train Based on Energy-saving Operation Optimization
abstract: To improve operation efficiency, more and more intelligent technologies are applied to the railway system. Compared with subway and high-speed rail, the intelligence level of the freight trains is relatively low, due to restrictions of the running environment. In this paper, a Connected Driver Advisory System(C-DAS) for freight trains is developed, which is mainly divided into two parts: onboard terminal and ground server. The onboard terminal provides a Man-Machine Interface(MMI), which can provide an energy-saving speed curve and control strategy for the train driver. Another function of the onboard terminal is to realize the train positioning. We use the position filtering algorithm based on electronic map to improve the positioning accuracy of the trains. The ground server and the onboard terminal are communicated by the 4G network. Different train energy-saving operation optimization algorithms can be integrated on the ground server. This paper proposes an Adaptive Differential Evolution(ADE) to provide an optimized train operation scheme for the onboard terminal. The simulation results have been compared with that of the traditional Differential Evolution(DE) algorithm, and the energy-saving ratio of ADE is improved by 12.1% to DE. Through field tests, it can be seen that the C-DAS can achieve precise positioning of the train, and provide train drivers with energy-saving train control schemes, which can improve the intelligence level of freight trains.

articleTitle: Research on the maintenance model for launch site ground equipment
abstract: Space launch site is a key infrastructure to support rocket launch. An overview of the characteristics of ground equipment maintenance at the launch site is provided in this paper, along with an analysis of the status of ground equipment maintenance and a discussion of the requirements for equipment maintenance as viewed from the perspective of maintenance staff. The equipment maintenance mode is proposed from the stages of equipment design, development and operation. The preliminary design of the maintenance flow in the operation stage is addressed, and it can be used as a guideline for constructing the ground equipment maintenance information system for the launch site.

articleTitle: Base-Arm Collaborative Planning of A Dual-Arm Mobile Robot for Truss Handling Tasks on the Moon
abstract: Dual-arm mobile robot has a good application prospect in various deep space exploration projects in the future. In this paper, a base-arm collaborative planning method for the truss handling task on the moon is proposed. Firstly, the kinematic model of the dual-arm mobile robot is built. For the task of grasping a truss, an optimization model for the location of robot base is built considering better dexterity and lower energy consumption. Then, a pareto solution set of optimal locations of robot base and moving trajectory which is feasible for the task can be calculated by NSGA-II algorithm. Simulation shows that the planning method can greatly improve the dexterity and energy consumption of a task compared with the no optimization method.

articleTitle: Construction and application of network security knowledge graph for power monitoring system
abstract: Facing the network security problem of power monitoring system, this paper studies the knowledge graph-based network security knowledge extraction and management method. In the entity recognition module, an entity recognition algorithm based on the idea of multi task learning is adopted, which decomposes the entity recognition process into entity boundary perception and entity classification to reduce the impact of error accumulation. Meanwhile, the introduction of comprehensive description information of entity categories into entity classification tasks can not only be widely used in general fields, but also be targeted to specific scenes in the field of power monitoring system. In the relation extraction module, based on the idea of multi-instance learning, the method of piecewise convolution neural network is employed, which reduces the impact of some instance annotation errors. The relation extraction method can extract text feature expression and inter entity structure information, which has a good effect on specialized field knowledge. Finally, based on the established knowledge graph, this paper studies the application problems of network security knowledge management and intelligent question answering of power monitoring system, which shows the effectiveness of knowledge graph technology in the field of network security management.

articleTitle: An Efficient Siamese Network for Pet Identity Verification
abstract: Vision-based pattern identification (such as face, fingerprint, iris etc.) has been successfully applied in human biometrics for a long history. However, pet identification is still a challenging problem due to the lack of labeled data and the existence of imbalanced sample classes in our available dataset. This paper overcomes the above difficulties and presents an efficient method for the 1 vs 1 pet identity verification mission launched by CVPR 2022 pet biometric. We use ArcFace method to select some hard samples at first. Then we make use of the hard samples obtained to construct positive and negative sample pairs. Finally, a Siamese network has been proposed to classify the sample pairs and trained to classify the image pairs of test sets. Meanwhile, in order to solve the problem that each class only with few samples in the training set, we propose an offline data augmentation strategy, which greatly improved the classification performance. Our methods achieve 88.3% AUC on test set 1 and 81.6% AUC on test set 2, outperforming some SOTA Re-ID methods and winning the thirteenth place in the challenge.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling of grid connected microgrid Based on Improved White Shark algorithm
abstract: Microgrid mode is a very important operation mode in the future power development. The in-depth study of the microgrid optimal scheduling strategy, through the optimal scheduling of the output of controllable micro sources, energy storage systems and other periods, is conducive to improving the utilization rate of distributed generation energy connected to the power system, ensuring the reliability and security of the system while meeting the basic needs of users for power supply, so that the system can achieve the effect of economic and environmental protection operation. In this paper, a multi-objective optimal dispatching model of microgrid is established, which aims at the economic operation cost and environmental treatment cost of the system, and an improved multi-objective white shark algorithm (MOWSO) based on nonlinear weight factor, Cauchy mutation and Levy flight is proposed. The multi-objective test function is used to verify the superiority of the improved algorithm, and the optimization model is solved with an example. The simulation results show that the model can effectively reduce the operation cost and environmental cost, and realize the economic operation of microgrid.

articleTitle: Research on Attention-Based Predictive Model in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Agent actions planning is a challenging problem in multi-agent reinforcement learning. Recent methods typically build their predictive models by full connection layers, but the shortage of utilizing action and observation information in complex multi-agent environment limits the performance of those methods. To address this issue, we propose a novel predictive model based on self-attention mechanism which can effectively use information in the environment. Specifically, we use the MADDPG algorithm to make a dataset where the input is the observations and actions and the output is the predicted observations and rewards. We also introduce the multi-head attention mechanism into the predictive model so that the predictive model can better combine different information for prediction. We perform extensive experiments to assess the proposed method and compare it with the representative baseline approach. Results demonstrate that our method outperforms competitors with higher accuracy in different tasks. Our implementation will be publicly available.

articleTitle: pH stablizing control of a neutral leaching process based on proximal policy optimization
abstract: Neutral leaching is the key process of zinc hydrometallurgy. The reasonable flow of waste acid added to make the terminal pH stable in a reasonable range is very important to improve the leaching rate and the removal rate of impurity ions. However, due to the fluctuation of inlet flow rate, feeding amount and composition change, there is great uncertainty in the process. And the stabling control of pH value is very challenging. In this paper, a pH optimization control algorithm based on proximal policy optimization (PPO) for leaching process is proposed. First, a nonlinear autoregressive (NARX) model is established based on process data for interacting with the agent. Then, the state space, action space and reward function are defined for the leaching process, and the strategies of action boundary setting and state normalization are adopted to ensure its learning performance. Finally, the experiments show that PPO controller can realize stabling control of pH value compared with manual experience. The optimal control framework based on deep reinforcement learning brings stability and intelligence to the zinc leaching process.

articleTitle: Target Recognition Based on Improved Fourier Descriptors
abstract: To address the problems of low recognition accuracy, slow computing speed, large memory consumption, high requirements for hardware facilities of traditional image target recognition algorithms and the deep learning method data set collection difficulties. In this paper, we propose an improved fast Fourier descriptors that can recognize target patterns quickly and accurately. The method first performs image enhancement and other pre-processing on the acquired image. Then uses the butterfly operation algorithm to accelerate the Fourier transform, calculates the Fourier descriptors of the target shape and improves the operation speed by reducing the number of key points of the target shape. Finally, the Fourier descriptors contours of the pattern to be detected and the template pattern are matched to determine the authenticity of the target recognition, and the OpenCV library is used for experimental simulation. The experimental results show that the method can accurately identify the target pattern and improve the recognition speed.

articleTitle: An LSTM and Encoder-Decoder-Based Approach for Runoff Prediction
abstract: Runoff time series are characterized by nonlinearity, complexity, and variability. Effective runoff prediction can improve the information and intelligence of local water resources management. To improve the accuracy of daily runoff prediction, this paper addresses the multidimensional data of hydrological data and multidimensional correlation meteorological factors to make multi-step prediction, and this paper proposes a sequence-to-series daily runoff prediction model based on encoder-decoder of long and short term memory network. To verify the validity of the model, six years of daily runoff data (2012-2017) and related meteorological factor data and three evaluation indexes (root mean square error, mean absolute error, and coefficient of determination) from the Punan hydrological station site in the Jiulong River basin of Fujian Province are selected for testing. The prediction results show that the proposed model has higher accuracy than the existing runoff prediction models such as gradient boosting (XGBoost), decision tree (DTA), support vector machine (SVR), convolutional neural network (CNN), recurrent neural network (RNN), and long-short time neural network (LSTM).

articleTitle: A particle swarm denoising algorithm applied to TDLAS direct absorption spectroscopy
abstract: TDLAS direct absorption spectroscopy detects gas concentration, the system white noise and interference fringes are one of the important factors that limit the detection accuracy and stability of the system severely. This paper reports a particle swarm denoising algorithm based on theory of spectral line shape, which is applied in direct absorption spectroscopy. The spectral line shape theory is the foundation that our algorithm calculates a fitness function, that conforms to the principle of minimum root mean square error in order the fitness function is correct. The update direction and position of particles are calculated by fitness value and preset learning factor. The data is updated iteratively to find the optimal solution. The algorithm can effectively eliminate the white noise of the system and the interference fringes generated by multi reflective light units so that improves the signal to noise ratio of the original signal.

articleTitle: Consensus Tracking Algorithm for Multi-Agent Systems with Binary-Valued Measurements
abstract: In this work, the tracking control problem of linear discrete time multi-agent systems(MAS) Under the conditions of binary-valued directed communication is studied. Unlike most studies, the transmitting signals in a network topology a binary-valued message with random noise to change its own state. A novel tracking convergence algorithm is designed: First, each follower obtains the estimated state of the neighbor through online algorithms. Second, each follower updates the status in time based on the estimates. We use a new Lyapunov function to analyze the stability of the MAS. In addition, agents can track the leader agent in time, and the fastest tracking rate can reach O(1/k) through the design parameters. Finally, the feasibility of the algorithm is demonstrated by simulation.

articleTitle: Research on particle swarm optimized image alignment algorithm based on improved SURF features
abstract: Image feature extraction and matching is an essential work in computer image processing. This technique aligns two or more images of the same scene obtained by different sensors under different or the same imaging conditions to determine the relationship between them. Based on the SURF algorithm, this paper adopts the local two-dimensional entropy to improve the uniqueness of the extracted feature points. Then the Euclidean distance in the traditional algorithm is changed to the Manhattan distance, and the distance evaluation function is introduced for pre-processing. Finally, the particle swarm algorithm is applied to optimize the feature point matching process. Through theoretical analysis and experimental contrast, the improved SURF algorithm has significantly improved both matching speed and accuracy, demonstrating the algorithm's reliability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Building Fire Simulation Analysis Based on Pyrosim and Revit
abstract: Once the fire occurs, it will often cause huge economic losses and a large number of casualties, which brings great challenges to the safety of the building when the fire occurs. Building fire has become a major issue that the society pays close attention to. In order to understand the smoke spreading law of building fire, the paper uses Pyrosim fire simulation software to simulate the fire scene. Focus on the research of smoke spread and development in the process of fire development and related laws, analysis of fire temperature distribution and visibility distribution

articleTitle: Hyperspectral inversion modeling of lactose content in milk based on CARS_VR
abstract: Achieving rapid and accurate determination of the components contained in milk is important for ensuring milk quality, preventing adulteration and safeguarding health. In this paper, we use hyperspectral technique to accurately measure the lactose content in milk. Herein we present a novel method based on hyperspectral inverse modeling utilizing Savitzky-Golay and first differentiation (SG_FD) to process the spectral data. The feature wavebands are filtered using competitive adaptive re-weighted sampling (CARS), and the lactose content in milk is predicted using an improved voting regression (VR). Upon comparing the predictions with other algorithms, it was determined that 39 feature wavebands screened with the CARS algorithm as input to the VR model had the best prediction effect, with a coefficient of determination $R_V^2$ of 0.9478 for the test set and a root mean square error RMSE<inf>V</inf> of 0.1382. It is evident from this paper that the improved VR inversion modeling algorithm presented in this paper has the potential to enhance both the overall performance of the inversion model and the prediction effectiveness of the model. The method can be applied to the detection of lactose content in milk and offers a new approach to determining the lactose content of milk.

articleTitle: A novel multi-target recognition method based on heatable marker for human following robots
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-target recognition method based on heatable marker which is consisted of a plurality of parallel-arranged carbon fibers is proposed. Every carbon fiber beam can be heated independently, and a binary rule is used to code the carbon fiber. The marker is worn around on the user’s waist so that robots will perceive obvious thermal radiation characteristics regardless whether the human is toward, lateral or turns his back to robots. A portable controller which is convenient for the human to carry around is designed to realize the temperature control. The distance between the robot and the human can also be obtained by a UWB model. Experiments show that the coded marker can be recognized and decoded accurately, and it can meet the requirement of multi-target detection tasks.

articleTitle: Ship Trajectory D-TCN Prediction Method Based on Satellite Remote Sensing Positioning Data
abstract: The trajectory prediction of the ground moving target is the premise of solving the intelligent observation task planning of remote sensing satellites. As a kind of moving target, the trajectories of ships do not have obvious periodicity in the short term, but the trajectories passing through a certain area in the long run are similar. Based on the historical remote sensing positioning data of ships, a prediction method D-TCN combining Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and temporal convolutional network (TCN) is proposed. First, the historical trajectory and current trajectory data of the ship are divided into trajectory, and then DBSCAN is used for trajectory clustering. The trajectory set containing the current trajectory end segment is used as the input of the TCN network to obtain the predicted trajectory. The simulation results show that the proposed method has higher prediction accuracy than traditional prediction models.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Ship Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOV5
abstract: Aiming at the high complexity and large amount of computation of ship target recognition, this paper proposes a detection algorithm of lightweight ship based on YOLOV5. The EagleEye pruning is used to compress the model and improve the speed of inference. α-EIoU loss function is proposed to accelerate model convergence and improve the accuracy of detection. The model is only 1.97MB after pruning, and the detection speed can reach 238FPS, which can achieve the real-time ship target recognition.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation of Machining Process Planning for Green Manufacturing
abstract: Given the variety of planning schemes and the elements that influence green manufacturing, a multi-level assessment index system based on five features is developed: machining time, cost of manufacturing, processing quality, resource consumption, and environmental conservation. After that, a fuzzy evaluation approach based on the Hierarchical Entropy Weight is constructed for evaluating process planning schemes. Using modified fuzzy operation principles, the full assessment of multi-process planning schemes is done, and the optimal one is finally determined. Finally, planning plans for vehicle parts are employed in order to validate their feasibility and efficacy of this approach. The results indicate that it is closer in accordance with the actual production and may give the most cost-effective and ecologically friendly processing scheme.

articleTitle: MSDR-Net: Multi-Scale Detail-Recovery Network for Single Image Deraining
abstract: Rain streaks vary in size, direction, and density, resulting in serious blurring and image quality degradation, which often directly affect the downstream visual tasks. At present, many end-to-end image removal networks have achieved good results, but image details are often lost during processing. Therefore, we propose a novel detail-recovery network to solve this problem. Unlike the existing works, we regard image rain removal and detail restoration as two different tasks simultaneously. Specifically, we use two encoder-decoder networks to extract rain streaks and detailed features and design different feature extraction blocks for two encoder-decoder networks. Due to the different receptive fields of feature layers at different scales, the information extracted at each scale is also different. The tasks of image rain removal and detail restoration are considered from the multi-scale feature level. To better respond to the image details and take full advantage of semantic information of multi-scale features, rain removal and image detail restoration are carried out at different scales. The proposed method has been validated on datasets to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Motion Control Analysis of Two-wheeled Robot Based on Newtonian Mechanics
abstract: Based on the basic mechanical principle, the motion state of the two-wheeled robot is analyzed and the model hypothesis is established. The pure pursuit algorithm is used to track the target path in the case of low-speed driving. For a given map, considering that the distance between the left and right wheels of the car cannot be ignored relative to the length of the map, the rasterization method is used to process the map, and after that, the obstacles in the map are reasonably expanded. Finally, the Dijkstra algorithm is used to plan the motion path of the robot. It can be seen from the experiments that Pure Pursuit algorithm can achieve path tracking well in the motion control of two-wheeled robots, and Dijkstra algorithm can achieve path planning well.

articleTitle: Mean Field Linear Quadratic Social Problem with a Major Player: a Direct Approach
abstract: This article studies a mean field social major-minor problem under linear quadratic framework. By the direct approach, the centralized optimal control laws and a series of forward-backward stochastic differential equations are derived first. Then, according to the mean field approximations, the decentralized feedback-type controls are designed and a system with BSDEs was achieved. By solving the BSDEs, the optimal decentralized controls can be obtained which are asymptotically and socially optimal.

articleTitle: Enhanced Couple Hierarchical Sliding Mode Control for Bridge Cranes with Matching Disturbances
abstract: Bridge crane plays an irreplaceable role in the industrial field, so the stabilization control of bridge crane is of great significance. However, improving the transient performance of the control system is still one of the major challenges in the research of the control method of bridge crane system. To solve this problem, a hierarchical sliding mode tracking control strategy with enhanced coupling is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the coupling signal is carefully designed, and then the coupling signal is introduced to transform the bridge system model accordingly. Finally, the tracking controller is designed to make the system state approach to the desired equilibrium point in finite time. Under the action of the controller designed in this paper, the trolley can fully restrain the load swing when it reaches the desired position. When sudden unmatched interference occurs, the system state can be quickly restored to the equilibrium point. The stability analysis is also given. Simulation results show that this strategy can improve the transient performance of the controller.

articleTitle: A New Chaotic System Based on New Memristor
abstract: This paper presents a new theoretical model of memristor, which contains a form of cubic polynomial taking absolute value. Baesd on this model, a new system is designed, which has periodic and chaotic dynamical characteristics, and there is constant chaos when some parameters varies. The reason for the formation of such characteristics is analyzed theoretically. Finally, to verify the correctness of the theory, an analog circuit is designed.

articleTitle: Attacks Detection and Disturbance Rejection Based on ESO/ROESO for Multiagent System
abstract: In this work, we consider the case, in view of the vulnerability of communication networks in leader-follower multi-agent systems, that is the attacker will launch False Data Injection Attacks against communication network. Consequently, to solve this, an effective detection mechanism for FDIAs which target at the communication network is established. In the meantime, for avoiding using false observation caused by FDIAs, Distributed Reduced-Order Extended State Observer (DROESO) is employed for mitigating the matched disturbance under contest environment because of its special principle. Finally, simulation example verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Study on safety boundary of launch bar considering steam catapult launch
abstract: In order to analyze the initial value range of the angle between the launch bar and deck in the safe steam catapult launch of carrier-based aircraft, the mathematical model of catapult launch is established. A method for solving the safety boundary of launch bar is proposed. By setting the initial steam pressure in the wet steam accumulator as 3.7MPa, 3.8MPa and 4.0MPa, three groups of steam catapult launch simulation tests of aircraft were carried out. The simulation results show that the steam pressure of the wet steam accumulator has a great influence on the safety boundary of the launch bar. The launch bar can always be within the safety boundary by adjusting the parameters of the wet steam accumulator; when the initial value of the launch bar is within the safe boundary, increasing the initial value of the launch bar can increase the angle of attack of leaving from carrier aircraft, which is conducive to the catapult launch; The research results can provide some theoretical reference for the design and test of launch bar and the formulation of safety criteria of launch bar.

articleTitle: Research on Reflector Navigation Algorithm and Optimization Smoothing Critical Path Trajectory
abstract: For mobile robots working in dense environments, navigation and path planning are crucial to understanding and reproducing human wayfinding thinking patterns. Firstly, this paper analyzed a hybrid SLAM navigation algorithm based on the reflector and laser constructed by the grid map method. Secondly, in the case of Kalman filter localization loss, this paper uses the generalized least squares inverse method to solve the nonlinear equations of the reflector to calibrate the localization information. Thirdly, the report used the RDP(Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm) algorithm to reduce the critical path points of the trajectory, which solves the problem of many path points in the traditional JPS algorithm. At the same time, used the optimal boundary NURBS curve algorithm to improve the robot trajectory quality. Finally, in large-scale simulation and physical environment, the navigation algorithm based on the reflector and the optimized smooth critical path trajectory algorithm was verified, proving the algorithm's effectiveness and accuracy in the complex domain.

articleTitle: Study on Terrain Aided Localization System of Underwater Glider Based on Particle Filter
abstract: The zigzag trajectory of underwater glider increases the application difficulty of TAL (Terrain Aided Localization) technology. In order to further improve the navigation ability of glider, the application of TAL in underwater glider is studied. This paper constructs a TAL system based on particle filter algorithm, and adjusts the particle set searching range and likelihood function in real time according to the running depth, so as to reduce the influence of measurement error and improve the localization robustness. Finally, the simulation research is carried out on a map of the Arctic seabed terrain. The results show that the TAL system has good robustness and can track the accurate position of the glider.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Ensemble Model for Short-Term Traffic Flow Prediction
abstract: Accurate and efficient short-term traffic flow prediction is critical for intelligent transportation systems. Traffic flow data has characteristics such as non-stationarity, dynamics, and spatial correlation, no particular method significantly outperforms all others. This paper focuses on the ensemble learning models which can benefit from multiple base models. Firstly, the spatiotemporal cross features are obtained through feature engineering strategies and feature selection strategies, and the lightweight decision tree algorithm LightGBM based on GBDT is used to combine these features to mine spatiotemporal correlation information. Secondly, graph convolution network (GCN) is used to mine the spatial correlations of traffic flow from different observation locations. Thirdly, long short-term memory network (LSTM) is applied to extract the temporal features of the traffic flow. The blending ensemble learning algorithm gives out the prediction results by integrating above three models. This proposed method is validated by using the PeMS04 dataset, and the results show that proposed method performs better than other methods in traffic flow prediction.

articleTitle: Adaptive Leader-following Practical Bipartite Consensus of Uncertain MIMO Dynamical Multi-Agent Systems over a Signed Directed Graph
abstract: This paper investigates the leader-following practical bipartite consensus problem of uncertain multi-input multi-output (MIMO) multi-agent systems (MASs) over a directed cooperation-competition network, where the followers are subject to matching uncertainties and the leader has an unknown bounded control input. An adaptive control algorithm is proposed to achieve the leader-following practical bipartite consensus, provided that the directed graph is structurally balanced and has a spanning tree rooted at the leader. Finally, a numerical example is performed to verify the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Adversarial Captcha with Three Target Detection Models
abstract: In order to distinguish whether the user is a human or a robot, prevent decryption of password, accounts and so on, three kinds of target detection model training for Adversarial Captcha are proposed. The process of training and evaluate-on of adversarial samples are described in detail in this paper. Depth target detection model is selected as attack model, and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) algorithm is applied to generate adversarial samples based on three models: YOLOv4, Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) and Faster Region-CNN (R-CNN). The samples are compared with clean samples under undirected attack. The results show that the captcha samples have successfully misled the neural network with high confidence, making them output incorrect results. The algorithm proposed in this paper can be used in many fields in the Internet to verify whether it is human or not.

articleTitle: Anomaly detection of gas flow meter based on improved GAN
abstract: As one of the core equipment in the gas industry, gas flow meter guides the operation and maintenance of gas companies and reflects the gas consumption habits of downstream users. Therefore, the anomaly detection of gas flow meter has important theoretical value and practical significance. However, the sensors of the gas flow meter are coupled with each other, and the collected data has the characteristics of difficult to collect negative samples. For the solution of the above challenges, an approach to unsupervised anomaly detection based on generative adversarial networks (GAN) is introduced in this paper. Firstly, after the flow meter signal is processed with the data screening, the Savitzky Golay (S-G) filter can filter out the noise from the raw data. The information between channels is captured by the feature attention module for improving the accuracy of the potential representation of samples, in addition, residual blocks are used to prevent the network degradation phenomenon in the deep network. Finally, the proposed model was demonstrated to be valid by using the actual user gas flow meter data. Compared with the current popular depth learning methods, the experimental results reveal that the proposed method can be very accurate in terms of ACC and F1 scores.

articleTitle: A Feedforward Neural Network Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm for Identification of User Stealing Electricity
abstract: In order to reduce the negative impact of electricity theft on power grid operation, improve the ability of electricity theft inspection and the accuracy of identifying electricity theft users, a feed-forward neural network model based on BFO-PSO is proposed to identify users behavior of stealing electricity. Based on the electricity consumption data of a city in recent four years, through feature extraction, four features that have a greater impact on electricity stealing behavior are obtained as input samples. A feedforward neural network recognition model based on BFO-PSO algorithm is constructed, and the optimal weight value of BP neural network model are calculated by using algorithm BFO-PSO. By comparing the recognition results of BP neural network model, genetic algorithm and the BFO-PSO algorithm, it is found that the feedforward neural network model based on BFO-PSO algorithm can better identify the power stealing users. The recognition accuracy is as high as 94%, and the training speed is increased by 5%. It is expected to be widely used in the power stealing user recognition..

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligent Load Forecast Method Using Image Based LSTM
abstract: Artificial intelligence method is used more and more widely in load forecasting, but the inputs of these methods are usually the raw time series. This paper presents a new artificial intelligence forecasting method using long short term memory (LSTM) and load image. Firstly, the raw time series load data is converted into load images. Then the load images are used as the input of LSTM forecasting model. Finally, the output image of the model is converted to load value as the final forecasting result. Experiments show that the method proposed has significantly improved the forecasting accuracy compared with the simple LSTM algorithm using the raw load time series as the input, and has certain engineering application value.

articleTitle: Differential Learning and Parallel Convolutional Network for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
abstract: Graph convolution network (GCN) has recently played a positive role in improving the accuracy of skeleton-based action recognition. Many GCN methods have reached a high accuracy. However, the lightweight of network model has recently become a major concern. Pointing at the problem, this paper introduces a lightweight network, a Differential Learning and Parallel Convolutional Network (DL-PCN), which is based on Semantics-Guided Neural Networks (SGN). The network is mainly composed of Differential Learning Module (DLM) and Parallel Convolutional Network Module (PCN). DLM is characterized by the feedforward connection, which improves the experiment accuracy. PCN can learn the multi-dimensional information of original skeleton data by the parallel connection of GCN and convolutional neural network (CNN). Considering the test accuracy of action recognition and network parameters, our network achieves the comparable performance on the NTU RGB+D 60 dataset and the NTU RGB+D 120 dataset.

articleTitle: Fast Fault Diagnosis for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells based on an Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Measurement
abstract: The proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) is considered as one of the most promising energy sources. For the large commercialization, it is necessary to improve the reliability and durability of PEMFCs with the fault diagnosis approach. This paper proposes an online fault diagnosis method for PEMFCs based on fast electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurement. Specifically, the periodic triangular wave is utilized as a disturbance current, and the PEMFC’s impedance spectrum is obtained through a fast Fourier transform (FFT). Then, the parameters of an improved equivalent circuit model are identified based on the nonlinear least squares method. After that, the support vector machine (SVM) with a one-vs-all strategy is established to diagnose four operation states. Experimental results show that the proposed fast fault diagnosis method can detect different faults accurately with strong generalization and robustness.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Driving Using Trapezoidal Decomposition
abstract: Trajectory planning is the core module of autonomous driving system and its main challenges lie in the decisions in non-convex space and the trade-off between safety, comfort and efficiency performances. This paper presents a noval framework that combines trapezoidal cell decomposition and convex optimization to generate optimal trajectories for autonomous vehicles in structured environment. The approach decoupes a 3D trajectory planning problem with timestamps information into 2D path planning and speed planning problems. Each 2D problem can be solved by a three-phase procedure. First, the trapezoidal cell decomposition is used to extract trapezoidal driving corridors. Second, the graph is constructed by adaptive sampling instead of inflexible uniform sampling, and the coarse path(or speed) and corresponding corridors are obtained by grpah search method. In the last phase, the coarse path(or speed) is optimized by piecewise Bézier polynomials and optimazation technique. The noval framework, called CB Planner, is especially useful for extracting corridors and generating coarse trajectory in complex environment. Experimental results show that compared with some state-of-art planners, this planner can generate higher quality trajectories and is more suitable for complex environments.

articleTitle: Combined Step-size Affine Projection M-estimator-like Algorithm
abstract: To improve the standard Affine Projection (AP) algorithm, which suffers from high steady-state error and poor convergence performance when dealing with unsteady impulse noise, a Combined Step-size Affine Projection M-estimator-like Algorithm (CS-APMLA) is proposed. CS-APMLA uses a convex combination method to combine multiple APMLA algorithms and adjusts the combination step according to the saturation characteristics to resolve the conflict between convergence speed and steady-state error, which can prevent the divergence of weight coefficients triggered by large-value impulse noise. From the theoretical derivation and simulation experiments, it can be shown that the convergence speed and noise reduction performance of the CS-APMLA algorithm is greatly improved compared with the APSA algorithm, VSS-APSA, and APMLA algorithm.

articleTitle: Defect detection for PV Modules based on the improved YOLOv5s
abstract: Cracks and fragments are common defects of photovoltaic (PV) modules, both of which can lead to severe degradation of PV power generation. Traditional fault diagnosis methods are difficult to accurately locate the defect regions in PV modules. In this paper, a developed YOLOv5s is proposed to achieve cracks and fragments detection of PV modules in the electroluminescent (EL) images. More Specific, a defect image dataset is constructed based on image preprocessing and data augmentation on 402 EL images. And a novel cross stage partial operation unit named C3_cbam and a novel spatial pyramidal pooling operation unit named SPP_eca are proposed respectively by combining with visual attention mechanism. Among which, C3_cbam is presented to develop C3_1 unit in YOLOv5s to help the network focus on critical regions in the image by incorporating spatial and channel information. SPP_eca is the improvement of SPP unit by enhancing channel attention to reduce the aliasing effects. The experiment results illustrate that the proposed algorithm achieves 0.923 mAP on the constructed defect image dataset, which has an accuracy increment of 3.3% compared with the original YOLOv5s algorithm. The algorithm also performs well compared to other state-of-art defect detection algorithms.

articleTitle: A Survey on Dynamic Graph Neural Networks Modeling
abstract: Compared with the Static Graph Neural Networks(SGNNs), the Dynamic Graph Neural Networks(DGNNs) have an additional temporal dimension, which can evolve along the time dimension, so DGNNs have more powerful and flexible modeling capabilities. DGNNs are widely used in the classical graph domain, such as social network recommendations, chemical molecular structure predictions and so on. They are also succeeding in areas such as social event prediction, video classification, traffic prediction. Although the advantages of DGNNs have been verified in various aspects, there are still relatively few relevant review studies. This paper describes the reason why DGNNs can process temporal data, which lays a foundation for subsequent understanding of various DGNNs models. Based on temporal models and GNN models, the whole design idea of DGNNs is provided for readers through detailed description of encoding and decoding process and link predictions of various DGNNs. Finally, we are dedicated to mining the commonness of DGNN framework from different task scenarios, and presenting a detailed DGNNs overview for readers.

articleTitle: An intelligent prognostic approach considering multi-mode degradation processes
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is of great importance for predictive maintenance of industrial equipment. The multi-mode of degradation processes and the relations among historical monitoring data are not taken into account comprehensively in the existing studies. To address this issue, a novel intelligent RUL prediction approach for multi-mode degradation processes considering the bidirectional memory is proposed in this paper. The mode classification is achieved via a universal change-point detection technique. The features are selected and fused by the distance correlation (DC) coefficient to obtain a clear representation of health condition. Bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) are introduced to enhance features and to establish the RUL prediction model. The effectiveness of the proposed method in accuracy is demonstrated by a case study of blast furnace.

articleTitle: DynamicVINS: Visual-Inertial Localization and Dynamic Object Tracking
abstract: SLAMMOT is a common solution for robust operation of SLAM in a dynamic environment while simultaneously estimating the motion of dynamic objects. Most of the current solutions are based on vision. In this paper, DynamicVINS, a VI-SLAMMOT system based on stereo vison and inertial sensor, can accurately estimate ego-motion and object motion in tightly-coupling. This paper makes full use of advanced deep learning work to provide good prior semantic information required for optimization, instance segmentation and 3D object detection. By combining 2D tracking and 3D object detection results, we implement a top-down data association method. Ego-motion, object motion, scene structure and object bounding boxes are optimized in a tightly coupled form within a sliding window. Compared with visual-only SLAMMOT, IMU information can obtain better prior pose and improve the accuracy of estimation. Finally, we evaluate the proposed system on KITTI dataset. The results show the excellent performance of the proposed system.

articleTitle: An improved event-trigger-based robust 6-DOF spacecraft formation control scheme under restricted communication
abstract: This paper addresses the robust six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) formation control problem for groups of spacecraft with constraints that include: restricted communication, unknown external perturbations, model uncertainties, and attitude orbit coupling. First, a Zeno-free trigger function is presented based on the event trigger mechanism to avoid continuous communication and save bandwidth resources; Then, the RBF neural networks are adopted to approximate the model uncertainties and external perturbations of the system; Furthermore, a distributed robust formation controller is designed and the coupling between the event trigger mechanism and neural networks is analyzed, and by designing Lyapunov functions, it is theoretically demonstrated that the formation error of spacecraft can converge to an arbitrarily small residual set. Finally, the simulation experiments are given to validate that the combination of the time-triggered mechanism and neural networks can effectively reduce the number of system controller updates, save communication bandwidth resources and weaken the impact of uncertainties on system stability.

articleTitle: Unknown Input Observer-based Finite-time Frequency Estimator for a Biased Multi-sinusoidal Signal
abstract: This paper proposes a novel finite-time parameter estimator for a multi-sinusoidal signal with a constant bias. Via the architecture of unknown input observer (UIO), a parameter model consisting of finite-time estimate of the sinusoid and its derivatives is rendered which can be applied with any existing adaptive identifier. Next, motivated by the recently developed Dynamic Regressor Extension and Mixing (DREM) method, we propose a novel parameter estimator guaranteeing the finite-time convergent property. Besides the finite-time property, the advantages such as modularity with systematic procedures, and fine-tunning gains implicitly manifest the effectiveness of our algorithm, which is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Obstacle-aware MDNets for Sampling Polytope Trees in Multi-robot Formation Path Planning
abstract: We present obstacle-aware MDNets (OMDNets) for path planning of multi-robot formation. In contrast to the RRT tree, each node of the OMDNets tree represents a feasible region for one or more formations. Moreover, each tree edge connects two feasible region centers that share at least one configuration. The construction of this tree requires node sampling and connecting. However, the existing method based on random sampling is inefficient due to the lack of information about obstacles. Also, the formation is not considered while connecting nodes. Therefore, OMDNets accept obstacle information as input and output the next practical point that generates an obstacle-free convex polytope. Moreover, a rapid checker based on the Minkowski approach is proposed for determining if two feasible regions can be connected.
